title: 隐而不露
blurb: 改写小说：如果当年姐妹被分开抚养，直到加冕日才重逢——）。

paras.en: “Presenting Princess Elsa of Arendelle!” Elsa stepped out of the shadow of her parents and into the sun.
paras.zh: “有请阿伦黛尔的艾莎公主！”艾莎从父母的身影后走出，步入阳光之中。

paras.en: Her people were waiting, welcoming her presence in the village square with thunderous applause.
paras.zh: 臣民们早已等候，以雷鸣般的掌声欢迎她在村镇广场上现身。

paras.en: There must have been hundreds of subjects gathered, young and old, waving flags with the royal family crest, throwing flowers, and cheering.
paras.zh: 聚集的臣民少说也有数百人，老少皆有，挥舞着绘有王室家徽的旗帜，抛撒鲜花，欢呼雀跃。

paras.en: Children sat high on their fathers’ shoulders, some people stood atop carriages, and others leaned out nearby windows.
paras.zh: 孩子们高高坐在父亲肩头，有人站在马车上，还有人从近旁的窗里探出身来。

paras.en: Everyone wanted to get a better look at the princess.
paras.zh: 每个人都想好好看一眼这位公主。

paras.en: Her parents were used to interacting with their kingdom, but at eighteen, she had only recently been invited to join them on official outings.
paras.zh: 父母早已习惯了与王国子民打交道，而十八岁的她，直到最近才被邀请一同出席正式活动。

paras.en: Truth be told, she still preferred to live life in the shadows, but duty called. “Welcome, Princess Elsa!” the people shouted.
paras.zh: 说实话，她仍更愿意活在阴影里，但责任在召唤。“欢迎你，艾莎公主！”人们高喊。

paras.en: Elsa and her parents were standing on a raised platform that had been constructed for the event.
paras.zh: 艾莎和父母站在一座为此次活动搭建的高台上。

paras.en: It overlooked the large courtyard outside the castle gates, giving her a good vantage point, but it also made her feel as if she was on display.
paras.zh: 高台俯瞰着城堡大门外宽敞的庭院，视野极佳，却也让她觉得自己像被展览一般。

paras.en: That was probably the point. “Look!
paras.zh: 或许这正是用意所在。“看！

paras.en: It’s Arendelle’s princess,” she heard a mother tell her small daughter. “Isn’t she beautiful?
paras.zh: ”那是阿伦黛尔的公主，“她听见一位母亲对年幼的女儿说。”她是不是很美？

paras.en: Offer her your gift.” The little girl was standing in front of the stage holding a bouquet of purple heather, which was Elsa’s favorite flower.
paras.zh: “把你的礼物献给她吧。”小女孩站在台前，手捧一束紫色石楠花——那是艾莎最爱的花。

paras.en: Every time she reached up to hand the bouquet to Elsa, she was knocked back by the crowd.
paras.zh: 每次她踮起脚想把花束递给艾莎，都被人群挤了回来。

paras.en: Elsa looked to her mother for guidance.
paras.zh: 艾莎望向母亲，寻求指引。

paras.en: The queen gave a small nod, and Elsa descended the steps, holding the bottom of her pale blue dress, which she had paired with a matching fitted jacket for the occasion.
paras.zh: 王后微微颔首，艾莎便提起淡蓝色礼服的下摆走下台阶——为这次场合，她配了一件同色系的合身短上衣。

paras.en: She and her mother shared similar light eyes, but she looked more like her papa with her light hair, which she usually wore in a braided bun at the nape of her neck. “Thank you for the lovely flowers,” Elsa told the child, graciously accepting the bouquet before stepping back up onto the platform to speak to the crowd.
paras.zh: 她与母亲有着相似的浅色眼眸，但浅金色的头发更像父亲——她通常把头发在脑后编成发髻。“谢谢你送的漂亮花，”艾莎对小女孩说，优雅地接过花束，再走回高台向人群致辞。

paras.en: Her father had been teaching her the unique power of presenting to a large group. “We are pleased you could all join us this afternoon as Axel Ludenburg unveils the sculpture of the royal family he has so graciously gifted our kingdom,” she began.
paras.zh: 父亲一直在教导她面向大众致辞的独特技巧。“今天下午，我们很高兴各位能齐聚于此，见证阿克塞尔·卢登堡揭幕他慷慨赠予王国的王室雕像，”她开场道。

paras.en: The people applauded. “One note before the unveiling: as Mr.
paras.zh: 人群鼓起掌。“揭幕前先说一句：卢登堡先生

paras.en: Ludenburg has spent years working on this piece, I suspect I will look much younger molded in bronze than I do standing before you today.” The crowd chuckled and Elsa glanced back at her father proudly.
paras.zh: ”耗费数年雕琢此作，我猜铸成铜像后的我，会比今日站在你们面前的我年轻许多。“人群轻笑起来，艾莎骄傲地回头望向父亲。

paras.en: That line had been her idea.
paras.zh: 这句台词是她想出来的。

paras.en: He gave her an encouraging smile. “His contribution to this kingdom is paramount.” Elsa smiled at the sculptor. “And now, without further ado, I would like to introduce Mr.
paras.zh: 他给了她一个鼓励的微笑。”他对本王国的贡献无可估量。“艾莎朝雕塑家微笑。”现在，闲话少说，我想介绍卢登堡先生

paras.en: Ludenburg.” Elsa moved aside to allow the older gentleman to join them. “Thank you, Princess.” Mr.
paras.zh: “艾莎退到一旁，让这位年长的绅士上前。”谢谢你，公主。“卢登堡先生

paras.en: Ludenburg bowed to her, his white beard almost touching his knees; then he turned to the crowd. “I am thankful to King Agnarr, Queen Iduna, and our fair princess, Elsa, for allowing me to create a sculpture in their honor.
paras.zh: ”朝她鞠躬，白胡须几乎拖到膝盖；随后他转向人群。“感谢安格瑞国王、伊杜娜王后，以及我们美丽的艾莎公主，允许我为他们塑像纪念。

paras.en: It is my hope that this piece will greet every guest who journeys from villages near and far to visit Arendelle’s castle and stand inside its gates.” He looked to his assistant, who dashed forward, untied the rope around the sheet concealing the sculpture where it stood in the middle of a fountain, and pulled it off. “May I present the royal family of Arendelle!” There was a loud gasp from the crowd, followed by rapt applause.
paras.zh: ”愿此作能迎接每一位远道而来的宾客，当他们来到阿伦黛尔城堡、立于城门之内时，首先见到它。“他看向助手，助手快步上前，解开蒙在雕像上的布单绳索——雕像立在喷泉中央——一把将布掀下。”请允许我介绍阿伦黛尔王室！“人群中爆出惊叹，继而是热烈的掌声。

paras.en: It was the first time the king, the queen, and Elsa had seen the completed sculpture.
paras.zh: 这是国王、王后与艾莎第一次见到完成的雕像。

paras.en: Elsa remembered sitting for Mr.
paras.zh: 艾莎记得曾为卢登堡先生

paras.en: Ludenburg’s sketches when she was around eleven, but she’d almost forgotten he’d been working on it until recently, when her father told her she’d be the one to speak at the royal engagement for its unveiling. “It’s beautiful,” Elsa told Mr.
paras.zh: ”画素描肖像，那时她大约十一岁，可直到前不久父亲说将由她在揭幕典礼上致辞，她才想起他一直在雕这尊像。“真美，”艾莎对卢登堡先生说。

paras.en: Ludenburg.
And she meant it.
paras.zh: 她是真心的。

paras.en: Seeing the bronze sculpture was like looking at a moment frozen in time.
paras.zh: 望着那尊铜像，仿佛看见了被时间冻结的一刻。

paras.en: Mr.
paras.zh: 卢登堡先生

paras.en: Ludenburg had molded the royal family perfectly.
paras.zh: ”把王室一家塑得惟妙惟肖。

paras.en: The youthful king looked regal in his crown and robe as he stood next to the beautiful queen in her tiara and fine dress.
paras.zh: 年轻的国王头戴王冠、身披王袍，神态威严，立于头戴小冠、身着华服的美丽王后身旁。

paras.en: Nestled between them was their only child, Princess Elsa of Arendelle, who looked much younger than her eighteen years.
paras.zh: 他们之间依偎着独女、阿伦黛尔公主艾莎，模样比她十八岁的年纪显得小得多。

paras.en: Seeing the image of her eleven-year-old self flooded Elsa with emotion.
paras.zh: 看到十一岁时的自己，艾莎心头涌起万千感触。

paras.en: Life in the castle had been lonely for her as an only child.
paras.zh: 作为独生女，城堡里的生活对她而言是孤独的。

paras.en: Her parents were busy with kingdom affairs, and while she had numerous studies, she still spent a lot of time roaming the empty rooms, watching the hours tick by.
paras.zh: 父母忙于国事，尽管她有许多功课，仍常常在空荡的房间里游荡，看着时光一点点流逝。

paras.en: Of course, her parents had found her playmates in their stewards’ and noblemen’s children, but it wasn’t the same as having a sibling to grow up with and confide in.
paras.zh: 当然，父母曾在管家与贵族子弟中为她找过玩伴，但那比不上有一个能一同长大、倾诉心事的兄弟姐妹。

paras.en: This was a weight she kept to herself, never wanting to burden her parents with her feelings.
paras.zh: 这是她独自承担的心事，从不愿以感伤拖累父母。

paras.en: Her mother had been unable to have more children after Elsa. “Isn’t the sculpture of us lovely, Mama?” Elsa asked.
paras.zh: 母亲在生下艾莎后便无法再育。“我们的雕像真好看，对吧，妈妈？”艾莎问。

paras.en: Her mother was standing quietly beside her.
paras.zh: 母亲静静地站在她身旁。

paras.en: Elsa watched her blue eyes take in every inch of the bronze statue before she gave a deep, almost inaudible, sigh.
paras.zh: 艾莎注视着母亲用蓝眼睛将铜像一寸寸看遍，随后发出一声深沉、几乎听不见的叹息。

paras.en: When she glanced at Elsa, her eyes seemed sad. “It truly is,” she said, squeezing her daughter’s hand. “It’s a lovely portrait of our family and who we are.
paras.zh: 当她看向艾莎时，眼中似有哀伤。“确实很美，”她握紧女儿的手说。“它把我们一家，以及我们的模样，都描绘得动人。

paras.en: Isn’t it?” she added to the king.
paras.zh: ”不是吗？“她又对国王说。

paras.en: For such a joyous occasion, her parents seemed slightly melancholy.
paras.zh: 如此欢庆的场合，父母却显得略带忧郁。

paras.en: Was it that the statue reflected a time when they were much younger?
paras.zh: 是因为雕像映出了他们年轻许多的时光吗？

paras.en: Were they sad to think how quickly time had passed?
paras.zh: 是想到了时光飞逝而伤感吗？

paras.en: Her father was always talking about the day when she would take the throne, even though he was still a vibrant king.
paras.zh: 父亲总念叨着她登基的那一天，尽管他自己仍是位精力充沛的国王。

paras.en: Elsa wondered what made them sad, but she kept her thoughts to herself.
paras.zh: 艾莎猜不透他们为何伤感，却把想法藏在心里。

paras.en: It wasn’t her place to question her parents in public. “Yes, it is quite the honor,” Papa replied, and looked at Elsa.
paras.zh: 在公开场合质疑父母不合她的本分。”是啊，这真是莫大的荣耀，“爸爸答道，望向艾莎。

paras.en: He seemed to want to say something more but held his tongue. “You should thank our subjects for coming, Elsa,” he said finally. “We’re hosting a dinner in Mr.
paras.zh: 他似还有话要说，却忍住了。”你该谢谢臣民们前来，艾莎，“他终于开口。”我们正为卢登堡先生

paras.en: Ludenburg’s honor back at the castle, so we must return and get ready to greet all our guests.” “Yes, Papa,” Elsa said, and did as she was told. “To Axel Ludenburg and his fine work!” the king said, holding his goblet high above the banquet table in the Great Hall.
paras.zh: “在城堡设宴，我们得回去准备迎接宾客了。”“好的，爸爸，”艾莎应声照做。“为阿克塞尔·卢登堡和他杰出的作品！”国王在大厅的宴席上高高举起酒杯。

paras.en: The other guests did the same. “To Axel!” they shouted, and clinked glasses.
paras.zh: 其他宾客纷纷效仿。“为阿克塞尔！”他们齐声高呼，碰杯致意。

paras.en: The food was plentiful, the company boisterous, and the seating at the long table at capacity.
paras.zh: 菜肴丰盛，席间喧闹，长桌座无虚席。

paras.en: The king had asked Lord Peterssen, his most trusted friend, to join them at the celebration.
paras.zh: 国王邀请了最信任的挚友彼得森勋爵共赴庆典。

paras.en: Mr.
paras.zh: 卢登堡先生

paras.en: Ludenburg’s family was there, too, having traveled by ship from the nation of Weselton, a longtime trade partner of Arendelle.
paras.zh: “的家人也来了，他们乘船从阿伦黛尔长久的贸易伙伴国韦塞尔顿远道而至。

paras.en: The Duke of Weselton had come with them, and seated himself next to Elsa. “And to Arendelle and Weselton!” the Duke added.
paras.zh: 韦塞尔顿公爵随行而来，在艾莎身旁落座。”也为阿伦黛尔和韦塞尔顿！“公爵补充道。

paras.en: He had a big mouth for such a small man.
paras.zh: 这小个子男人，嘴倒是不小。

paras.en: Elsa couldn’t help noticing he was at least a foot shorter than most guests at the table when he stood up. “Long may our countries grow together and prosper!” “To Arendelle and Weselton!” everyone echoed.
paras.zh: 艾莎不禁注意到，他站起来时比席上多数宾客矮了至少一英尺。”愿两国共同成长、繁荣昌盛！“”为阿伦黛尔和韦塞尔顿！“众人齐声应和。

paras.en: Elsa clinked glasses with her mother. “I’m so glad we finally have a chance to dine together,” the Duke said to Mama as the supper plates were taken away and the staff prepared to bring out dessert. “It is a pleasure to meet the princess and witness Arendelle’s bright future.” His brow furrowed. “I’ve long noticed she doesn’t come to many public events.” Elsa politely returned his smile but said nothing.
paras.zh: 艾莎与母亲碰了杯。”真高兴我们终于有机会共进晚餐，“撤去主菜、侍者准备上甜点时，公爵对妈妈说。”能见到公主、见证阿伦黛尔光明的未来，实为幸事。“他皱起眉头。”我早注意到她很少出席公开活动。“艾莎礼貌地回以微笑，并未作声。

paras.en: One of the roles of being a princess, as Mama kept reminding her, was to listen to people but wait to speak till something important needed to be said. “Elsa is so busy with her studies that we haven’t asked her to join us on many public outings yet,” Mama told him, and looked at Mr.
paras.zh: 身为公主的职责之一，正如妈妈常提醒的，是倾听他人、重要的话才说。”艾莎学业繁忙，我们还没怎么请她参加公开活动，“妈妈对他说，目光转向卢登堡先生

paras.en: Ludenburg. “But of course, we couldn’t have her miss the unveiling of our family sculpture.
paras.zh: ”。“不过当然，我们可不能让她错过自家雕像的揭幕。

paras.en: That is what this whole evening is all about: family.” Elsa covered her mouth to hide her smirk.
paras.zh: ”今晚的一切，核心就是家人。“艾莎捂住嘴，藏起一抹笑意。

paras.en: Her mother had a knack for keeping conversations focused.
paras.zh: 母亲总能把话题拢在正轨上。

paras.en: This was Elsa’s first time meeting the Duke of Weselton.
paras.zh: 这是艾莎第一次见到韦塞尔顿公爵。

paras.en: Already she could tell she preferred the Duke of Blakeston, who had kind eyes and always came to the castle with pocketfuls of chocolate, which he snuck to the princess during particularly boring dinner discussions.
paras.zh: 她已经能分辨出，自己更中意布莱克斯顿公爵——他眼神和善，来城堡时总揣着满口袋巧克力，在特别无聊的宴谈中偷偷塞给公主。

paras.en: Correction: important negotiations .
paras.zh: 更正：是”重要谈判“。

paras.en: As her mother kept reminding her, she needed to be ready for the throne when her time came.
paras.zh: 正如母亲常提醒的，时日到来时，她得为登基做好准备。

paras.en: These days she divided her time between lessons on handwriting, science, and statecraft with her governess, and Papa’s meetings.
paras.zh: 如今她的时间分在两部分：与家庭教师练习书法、科学与治国之道，以及旁听爸爸的会议。

paras.en: She was also now old enough to attend the banquets held at the castle, of which there were many.
paras.zh: 她如今也已到了能参加城堡宴会的年纪，这样的宴会可不少。

paras.en: Gone were the days when she was trotted out to say hello to guests, then sent to another room to have supper.
paras.zh: 那种被领出来向宾客问好、随即被打发去别处吃晚饭的日子，已经一去不返。

paras.en: Life was less lonely, but she still longed for someone her own age to confide in.
paras.zh: 生活没那么孤独了，可她仍渴望有个同龄人能说知心话。

paras.en: The days of hosting playmates were long over. “Agreed, agreed!
paras.zh: 招待玩伴的日子早过去了。”说得对，说得对！

paras.en: But she is too much of an asset to be locked away.” The Duke pounded the table as if to make a point.
paras.zh: “可她这样的人才，关在家里太可惜了。”公爵捶着桌子，像要强调什么。

paras.en: He moved so much when he talked his toupee kept flipping up on the back of his head. “Fine point, Your Grace,” said Lord Peterssen, joining the conversation. “She’s a young lady now and ready to take part in the kingdom’s conversations.” Elsa smiled at him.
paras.zh: 他说话时动作太大，假发总在脑后翘起。“说得好，公爵大人，”彼得森勋爵加入谈话，“她如今是位少女了，已准备好参与王国的事务。”艾莎朝他微笑。

paras.en: Papa and Lord Peterssen were so close he wasn’t just an advisor; he was family.
paras.zh: 爸爸与彼得森勋爵亲密无间，他不只是谋臣，更是家人。

paras.en: Elsa had always thought of him like an uncle.
paras.zh: 艾莎一向把他当叔叔看待。

paras.en: And like an uncle, he had warned Elsa before the dinner about the Duke’s tendency to pry. “Exactly!” the Duke agreed. “Princess Elsa, I’m sure your studies taught you a lot about fjords and how instrumental they can be.” Elsa nodded. “Well, in Weselton, it was my grandfather who discovered the first fjord.
paras.zh: 正如叔叔一般，晚宴前他提醒过艾莎，公爵爱打探。“正是！”公爵附和。“艾莎公主，想必你的学业让你对峡湾颇有了解，也懂它们多么重要。”艾莎点头。“在韦塞尔顿，发现第一处峡湾的正是我祖父。

paras.en: It is because of him that we…” The Duke droned on and on till Lord Peterssen cleared his throat. “Fascinating, Your Grace!
paras.zh: ”正因如此，我们……“公爵喋喋不休，直到彼得森勋爵清了清嗓子。”真有趣，公爵大人！

paras.en: Perhaps we can finish this conversation later?
paras.zh: “或许我们稍后再聊？

paras.en: I believe dessert is being served.” He turned away before the Duke could interrupt him. “Mr.
paras.zh: ”甜点该上来了。“他趁公爵插话前转过身去。”卢登堡先生

paras.en: Ludenburg, I hope you are still hungry!” As if on cue, the staff appeared at the doors with platters of fruit and sweets, which they placed on the table. “We have all these treats and more in Weselton,” the Duke piped up as he helped himself to a piece of cake and two cookies.
paras.zh: “希望你还没吃饱！”仿佛收到信号，侍者端着水果与甜点的托盘出现在门口，将食物摆上桌。“在韦塞尔顿，这些点心我们都有，还有更多，”公爵插嘴道，顺手拿了一块蛋糕和两块饼干。

paras.en: Elsa knew it was wrong of her to think it, but “Weselton” sounded a lot like “Weaseltown,” and the Duke did have a weasel-like way about him.
paras.zh: 艾莎知道自己不该这么想，可“韦塞尔顿”听上去活像“Weaseltown”（黄鼠狼镇），而公爵身上确有股黄鼠狼般的做派。

paras.en: She glanced at Papa.
paras.zh: 她瞥了爸爸一眼。

paras.en: Had he ever noticed this connection between the Duke and his country’s name?
paras.zh: 他是否也曾察觉公爵与其国名之间的这层关联？

paras.en: His thoughts were always veiled.
paras.zh: 他的心思总是深藏不露。

paras.en: At the moment, he was having a side conversation with Mr.
paras.zh: 此刻，他正与卢登堡先生

paras.en: Ludenburg’s wife.
paras.zh: “的妻子在一旁低声交谈。

paras.en: Lord Peterssen was speaking with the sculptor himself about his next project, which left the Duke, Mama, and Elsa unengaged. “Your Majesty, you have a lovely daughter,” the Duke said, making Elsa immediately feel guilty about her thoughts. “She will make a fine queen.” “Thank you,” Mama said. “She truly will.” “My parents have taught me well,” Elsa added, smiling at Mama. “When my day comes, I know I’ll be ready to lead Arendelle.” The Duke looked at her with interest. “Yes!
paras.zh: 彼得森勋爵正与雕塑家本人聊他的下个计划，于是公爵、妈妈和艾莎便没了话说。”陛下，您有个可爱的女儿，“公爵说，令艾莎立刻对自己的念头感到愧疚。”她会是一位出色的女王。“”谢谢，“妈妈说，”她一定会的。“”父母把我教得很好，“艾莎朝妈妈微笑着补充，”时日到来，我必能带领阿伦黛尔。“公爵饶有兴致地看着她。”是啊！

paras.en: Yes!
paras.zh: “是啊！

paras.en: I’m sure.
paras.zh: ”我确信。

paras.en: It’s just a shame you’re the only heir.
paras.zh: “只可惜你是唯一继承人。

paras.en: Why, in the Southern Isles, the king has thirteen sons in line for the throne.” Elsa clutched her goblet on the table to keep from saying something she would regret.
paras.zh: ”你瞧，在南境群岛，国王有十三个儿子排队等王位呢。“艾莎攥紧桌上的酒杯，免得说出会后悔的话。

paras.en: Strangely, the goblet was ice cold. “Sir, I hardly think that’s—” Mama cut her off. “What Elsa is trying to say is, that is a lot of heirs.” Mama was seemingly unperturbed, having been asked about this before. “My fate was to have only one child, but the world is full of surprises.” She looked at Elsa, her eyes shiny. “I know that she will be fine in the future.” “Our kingdom only needs one strong leader,” Elsa added, her voice firm. “They already have that in me.” The Duke frowned. “Yes, but if anything were to prevent you from taking the throne—” “We are fully prepared to lead Arendelle into the future, Duke, I assure you,” Mama said with a smile.
paras.zh: 奇怪，那酒杯冰冰凉凉。”先生，我觉得这未免——“妈妈打断她。”艾莎想说的是，那可真够多的继承人。“妈妈似乎不为所动，这类问题她早被问过。”我的命数只养得起一个孩子，但世界充满惊喜。“她望向艾莎，眼里闪着光。”我知道她将来会好好的。“”我们的王国只需要一位坚强的领袖，“艾莎语气坚定地补充，”而那个人已经是我了。“公爵皱起眉。”是，可万一有什么阻碍你登基——“”我们完全准备好带领阿伦黛尔走向未来了，公爵，我向您保证，“妈妈微笑着说。

paras.en: The Duke scratched his head, his toupee shifting slightly.
paras.zh: 公爵挠了挠头，假发微微挪了位。

paras.en: He looked from the queen to Elsa over his spectacles. “She will be of age in a few years.
paras.zh: 他从眼镜上方将目光从王后移到艾莎身上。”再过几年她就成年了。

paras.en: Are there any potential suitors on the horizon?
paras.zh: “可有潜在的求婚人选在望？

paras.en: A match between our two nations or with another trade partner could be prosperous indeed.” Elsa stared at the napkin in her lap.
paras.zh: ”我国与贵国，或与其他贸易伙伴联姻，定能带来繁荣。“艾莎盯着膝上的餐巾。

paras.en: She felt her cheeks burning. “Elsa has plenty of time to find a suitor,” Mama said. “For now, we just want our daughter to focus her attention on her duties to this kingdom.” That statecraft test her governess was giving her in the morning was a lot more pressing than finding a suitor. “Thank you for thinking of me, Your Grace,” Elsa added. “When I do find a suitor, I’m sure you’ll be one of the first to know.” She was being wry, but the Duke seemed pleased with her response.
paras.zh: 她觉得脸颊发烫。”艾莎有的是时间找对象，“妈妈说，”眼下我们只想让女儿专心履行对王国的职责。“家庭教师明早要考的治国测验，可比找对象紧迫多了。”谢谢您替我操心，公爵大人，“艾莎补了一句，”等我真找着了，一定第一个通知您。“她本是讽刺，公爵却似乎很满意这回答。

paras.en: Mama gave her a reproachful look, but Elsa couldn’t help herself.
paras.zh: 妈妈投来责备的一瞥，可艾莎忍不住。

paras.en: When the Duke finally retired and Mr.
paras.zh: 公爵终于告退，卢登堡先生

paras.en: Ludenburg and his family had said their goodbyes, the king, the queen, and Elsa headed to their private chambers. “You handled yourself well,” Mama told her. “You were excellent at conversation and you impressed the Duke with your knowledge of trade negotiations.” “He looked surprised I knew as much as I did,” Elsa said.
paras.zh: ”与家人道别后，国王、王后与艾莎走向各自的寝宫。“你表现得很好，”妈妈对她说，“谈吐得体，还用贸易谈判的见识让公爵刮目相看。”“他似乎惊讶我知道这么多，”艾莎说。

paras.en: Her shoulders felt tense, as if she’d been carrying the weight of her kingdom on them all evening.
paras.zh: 她肩膀紧绷，仿佛整晚都扛着王国的重量。

paras.en: She was starting to get a headache and she longed for the quiet of her room. “I’m very proud of you,” Papa said, letting his guard down for the first time all evening.
paras.zh: 她开始头疼，渴望回到房间独享安静。“我为你骄傲，”爸爸说，那是整晚第一次卸下防备。

paras.en: He smiled at Mama and placed his hand on her arm.
paras.zh: 他对妈妈微笑，将手搭在她臂上。

paras.en: She loved watching her parents together.
paras.zh: 她爱看父母相守的模样。

paras.en: They still looked so in love.
paras.zh: 他们看上去仍如此相爱。

paras.en: It was hard not to envy the connection they had with each other. “You will make an excellent queen someday, Elsa,” he added. “Thank you, Papa,” she replied, but didn’t think anything of it.
paras.zh: 很难不羡慕他们之间的羁绊。“你将来会是一位出色的女王，艾莎，”他补充。“谢谢爸爸，”她答道，却没往心里去。

paras.en: Becoming queen was a lifetime away.
paras.zh: 成为女王，那是遥遥无期的事。

paras.en: “On Mondays, subjects are invited to meet with your mother and me to discuss any concerns they have for the kingdom.
paras.zh: “周一，臣民受邀与我和你母亲会面，商讨他们对王国的任何关切。

paras.en: I think it’s best if we keep a standing appointment.
paras.zh: ”我认为最好把这个约定固定下来。

paras.en: You and Lord Peterssen can meet with them and listen to their concerns.
paras.zh: “你和彼得森勋爵可以接见他们，倾听他们的忧心事。

paras.en: Be compassionate and considerate and promise to pass any grievances on to us when we return.
paras.zh: ”要心怀悲悯、体贴周到，并承诺待我们回来后，将任何不满转达给我们。

paras.en: Now, on Tuesdays…Elsa?
paras.zh: “那么，周二……艾莎？

paras.en: Are you listening?” “Yes, Papa,” Elsa said, but in truth her mind was elsewhere.
paras.zh: ”你在听吗？“”在的，爸爸，“艾莎说，其实她心思早已飘远。

paras.en: They were sitting in the library, discussing his weekly schedule, but she was distracted.
paras.zh: 他们坐在图书室里，商量他的每周日程，可她走了神。

paras.en: She’d spent a lot of time in that room over the years, and even as a little girl, she had felt her mind wander when she was around all those books.
paras.zh: 这些年来她在那间屋子待过许久，即便还是小女孩，置身书海时她也会心神游荡。

paras.en: The dark room was lined with shelves filled with books from floor to ceiling.
paras.zh: 昏暗的房间里，书架沿墙而立，从地板直抵天花板。

paras.en: Her father was always reading and had several books open on the desk.
paras.zh: 父亲总在读书，书桌上摊着好几本。

paras.en: That day he was looking at one that didn’t seem to be written in their language.
paras.zh: 那天他正在看一本，似乎不是用他们的语言写成的。

paras.en: It was filled with symbols and drawings of trolls.
paras.zh: 书中满是符号与地精的图样。

paras.en: She longed to know what her father was studying, but didn’t ask.
paras.zh: 她渴望知道父亲在研读什么，却没开口问。

paras.en: What he wanted her to know right then was what to do in his and Mama’s absence.
paras.zh: 他此刻想让她知道的，是他和妈妈不在时该怎么做。

paras.en: They were scheduled to go on a diplomatic voyage for at least two weeks in a few days’ time.
paras.zh: 他们定于几天后启程外交远航，至少两周。

paras.en: Elsa couldn’t remember when they’d ever been away that long before.
paras.zh: 艾莎记不起他们曾离家如此之久。

paras.en: There was a part of her that was nervous.
paras.zh: 她心底有一丝不安。

paras.en: She knew she would keep busy between her own work and her father’s appointments, but she missed her parents already and they hadn’t even left yet.
paras.zh: 她知道自己会在自己的功课与父亲的约见间忙碌，可她已经想念父母，尽管他们还未动身。

paras.en: Her father folded his hands in his lap and gave her a small smile. “What’s the matter, Elsa?” Even when it was just the two of them, her father still seemed like a king.
paras.zh: 父亲双手交叠膝上，朝她浅浅一笑。”怎么了，艾莎？“即便只有他们俩，父亲仍透着国王的气度。

paras.en: It wasn’t just that he always dressed the part, in his uniform with a multitude of medals, and with the Arendelle crest hanging from his neck.
paras.zh: 不只因他总穿得合身份——制服上缀满勋章，颈间垂着阿伦黛尔家徽。

paras.en: Whether he was speaking to a foreign dignitary or thanking one of the castle workers, his manner always seemed royal.
paras.zh: 无论与外国使节交谈，还是向城堡仆人致谢，他的举止总透着王者的风范。

paras.en: He was powerful and in control even when he didn’t have to be—like during a game of chess with his only daughter.
paras.zh: 他强大而稳掌全局，即便不必如此时——比如和独生女下棋。

paras.en: She still felt shy sometimes.
paras.zh: 她有时仍会害羞。

paras.en: Was that just who she was, or was it that she didn’t have many people her age to converse with?
paras.zh: 那是她的本性，还是因为她少有同龄人可倾诉？

paras.en: Speaking to the large crowd at Mr.
paras.zh: 在卢登堡先生

paras.en: Ludenburg’s event had made her nervous.
paras.zh: ”的活动上面对众人，曾让她紧张。

paras.en: Her father never looked uneasy.
paras.zh: 父亲从不会显得局促。

paras.en: Did that kind of confidence come with time? “Nothing,” Elsa lied.
paras.zh: 那种自信是随时间而来的吗？“没什么，”艾莎撒谎道。

paras.en: It wasn’t possible to put all she was thinking into a few words. “Ah, but it is something.” He leaned back in his chair and studied her closely. “I know that look.
paras.zh: 她想的全装不进几句话里。“啊，可这分明是'有什么'。”他靠回椅背，仔细打量她。“我认得这神情。

paras.en: You are thinking about something.
paras.zh: ”你在想什么。

paras.en: Your mother says I get a far-off look in my eye when I’m doing the same thing.
paras.zh: “你母亲说，我做同样的事时眼里也会飘向远方。

paras.en: You, my child, are a lot like me.” “Really?” Elsa brushed an invisible strand of hair out of her eyes.
paras.zh: ”我的孩子，你很像我。“”真的吗？“艾莎拂开眼前一缕并不存在的发丝。

paras.en: She was proud to take after Papa.
paras.zh: 她以像爸爸为荣。

paras.en: She adored her mother and loved spending time with her, but often she couldn’t tell what her mother was thinking.
paras.zh: 她敬爱母亲，喜欢和她相处，却常猜不透母亲在想什么。

paras.en: Sometimes Mama would lose her train of thought when she came into Elsa’s room, or start saying something and abruptly stop.
paras.zh: 有时她走进艾莎房间，妈妈会突然断了思路，或话说到一半戛然而止。

paras.en: There was a lingering sadness about her that Elsa could never put her finger on.
paras.zh: 她身上有种挥之不去的哀伤，艾莎始终说不清道不明。

paras.en: Take that day, for example.
paras.zh: 就拿那天来说。

paras.en: For years, Mama had always disappeared for one full day every other month.
paras.zh: 多年来，妈妈每隔一个月总会消失一整天。

paras.en: Elsa had no clue where she went, and neither Papa nor Mama ever explained.
paras.zh: 艾莎毫不知她去了哪，爸爸和妈妈也从未解释。

paras.en: This time, Elsa couldn’t help herself.
paras.zh: 这一回，艾莎忍不住了。

paras.en: She was tired of the secrets, so she finally got the courage to ask Mama if she could join her on her outing.
paras.zh: 她厌倦了秘密，终于鼓起勇气问妈妈，能否陪她一同出门。

paras.en: Mama looked surprised, then worried, then apologetic. “I wish I could take you, darling, but this is something I must do alone.” She had touched Elsa’s cheek, her eyes welling with tears, which only confused Elsa more. “I wish you could come.” Yet she had gone alone.
paras.zh: 妈妈先惊讶，继而担忧，最后歉疚。”亲爱的，我多想带你去，可这事我必须独自完成。“她抚过艾莎的脸颊，眼里噙满泪，只让艾莎更困惑。”我多希望你能来。“可她还是独自去了。

paras.en: With Papa, things were different. “I’m not thinking of anything important, Papa.
paras.zh: 和爸爸相处则不同。”我没在想什么要紧事，爸爸。

paras.en: Really.” “Something is on your mind, Elsa,” he insisted. “What is it?” She felt foolish saying she didn’t want them to go away, but that was part of it.
paras.zh: “真的。”“你心里有事，艾莎，”他坚持道，“是什么？”说不想让他们离开显得傻气，可那确是其中一部分。

paras.en: With them gone, Arendelle was in her hands.
paras.zh: 他们离去，阿伦黛尔便交到她手中。

paras.en: Yes, the advisors and Lord Peterssen were there if anything important needed to be taken care of, but she was the face of the kingdom in their absence, and she could feel the weight of that pressing on her.
paras.zh: 没错，若有要事，自顾问与彼得森勋爵在，但她才是他们缺席时王国的门面，她能感到那份重量压在肩头。

paras.en: Before long, they’d return and life would be as it had been before, but this trip seemed like a steadfast reminder that someday she would have to rule on her own.
paras.zh: 不久他们便会归来，生活如常，可这趟远行像坚定的提醒：终有一天她得独自统治。

paras.en: The thought was terrifying. “Elsa?” Two weeks alone in this large castle.
paras.zh: 这念头令人胆寒。“艾莎？”在这座大城堡里独处两周。

paras.en: Elsa wasn’t sure she could bear it. “Do you really have to go?” she asked.
paras.zh: 艾莎不确定自己撑不撑得住。“你们非走不可吗？”她问。

paras.en: She couldn’t help it. “You’ll be fine, Elsa,” he promised.
paras.zh: 她忍不住了。“你会没事的，艾莎，”他承诺。

paras.en: There was a knock on the door. “Your Majesty?” Kai entered.
paras.zh: 传来敲门声。“陛下？”凯走了进来。

paras.en: He’d been working in the castle since before Elsa was born.
paras.zh: 他在城堡当差，比艾莎出生还早。

paras.en: While the king ran the kingdom, Kai ran the castle.
paras.zh: 国王管王国，凯管城堡。

paras.en: He knew where everything and everyone were always supposed to be.
paras.zh: 他清楚每样东西、每个人该在何处。

paras.en: He was such an important part of the king’s and queen’s lives that he even had a room adjacent to their chambers.
paras.zh: 他在国王与王后的生活中如此重要，连居室都紧邻他们的寝宫。

paras.en: Kai pulled at a loose thread on the jacket of the green suit he always wore. “The Duke of Weselton is here to see you.” “Thank you.
paras.zh: 凯扯了扯常穿的绿西装外套上一根松线。“韦塞尔顿公爵来见您。”“谢谢。

paras.en: Please tell him I’ll meet him in the council chambers shortly,” Papa said. “Yes, Your Majesty.” Kai smiled at Elsa and disappeared.
paras.zh: ”请告诉他我稍后在议事厅见他，“爸爸说。”遵命，陛下。“凯朝艾莎一笑，转身离去。

paras.en: Papa turned to her. “You look like you have more to say.” Too much to share in just a few short moments. “I was trying to decide what to serve at the session with the subjects,” Elsa said instead. “Do you serve food?
paras.zh: 爸爸转向她。”你似乎还有话要说。“太多话，片刻说不尽。”我方才在想接见臣民时该上些什么点心，“艾莎改口道。”你们还备吃的？

paras.en: I think it would be nice to nourish them after their journey to the castle to see us.
paras.zh: “我想他们远道来城堡见我们，款待些吃食挺好。

paras.en: Don’t you think?” He smiled. “I think that’s a splendid idea.
paras.zh: ”你不觉得吗？“他微笑。”我觉得这主意妙极了。

paras.en: I’ve always been fond of your krumkake cookies.” “ My cookies?” Elsa couldn’t recall ever baking for her father. “You’re giving me credit for something Olina must have made, but I’m happy to request them.” Olina was in charge of the kitchen in the castle and oversaw all the workers.
paras.zh: “我一直喜欢你的krumkake（脆卷饼干）。”“我的饼干？”艾莎记不得曾为父亲烤过。“你把这功劳算在我头上，定是奥丽娜做的，不过我很乐意去要。”奥丽娜掌管城堡厨房，督管所有厨工。

paras.en: When Elsa was a girl, she had often snuck away to the kitchen to sit with her.
paras.zh: 艾莎小时候，常溜去厨房陪她坐。

paras.en: She hadn’t done that in a long time.
paras.zh: 她已很久没这么做了。

paras.en: And she didn’t remember ever baking cookies.
paras.zh: 她也记不得自己烤过饼干。

paras.en: Papa’s brow furrowed. “Right.
paras.zh: 爸爸皱起眉。“对。

paras.en: Still, they’d be delicious.
paras.zh: ”不过，那一定很好吃。

paras.en: Maybe Olina will make them for our guests.” Elsa started to rise. “Is there anything else, Papa?” “Yes.” He stood up. “Before you go, there is something I wanted to give you.
paras.zh: “也许奥丽娜会为宾客做。”艾莎起身。“还有别的吗，爸爸？”“有。”他站起。“你走前，我想给你样东西。

paras.en: Follow me, if you don’t mind.” Elsa followed Papa to her parents’ bedroom and watched as he walked to a bookcase along one wall and pressed on one of the books.
paras.zh: ”随我来，若不介意。“艾莎跟着爸爸来到父母卧室，看他走向靠墙的书柜，按下一本书。

paras.en: The entire wall opened like a door.
paras.zh: 整面墙像门一样打开。

paras.en: A small darkened chamber was behind it.
paras.zh: 后面是一间昏暗的小密室。

paras.en: Elsa strained to see where he was going, but Papa didn’t ask her to follow.
paras.zh: 艾莎努力想看清他去了哪，爸爸却没叫她跟上。

paras.en: The castle was full of hidden hallways and rooms like that one.
paras.zh: 城堡里满是这类隐秘的通道与房间。

paras.en: Papa and she had played hide-and-seek in a few once upon a time, but she knew now they were meant to shuttle the royal family to safety if there was an invasion.
paras.zh: 爸爸曾和她在一些密道里捉迷藏，可她如今明白，它们是入侵时护送王室脱险的。

paras.en: Moments later, her father came out with a large green wooden box.
paras.zh: 片刻后，父亲捧出一个绿色大木箱出来。

paras.en: It was the size of a breakfast tray and was hand-painted with white and gold rosemaling of the golden crocus, Arendelle’s official flower.
paras.zh: 它约有早餐托盘大小，手工绘着阿伦黛尔国花——金色藏红花的白金玫瑰花饰。

paras.en: The top of the box had a beautiful arch to it. “I want you to have this.” He placed the box on the table in front of her.
paras.zh: 箱盖呈优美的拱形。”我想把它交给你。“他将箱子放在她面前桌上。

paras.en: Her fingers traced the gold family crest etched into the rounded top.
paras.zh: 她的指尖抚过圆盖上蚀刻的金色家徽。

paras.en: The box was identical to the lockbox her father kept on his desk and carried with him to meet with his advisors.
paras.zh: 这箱子与父亲置于书桌、携去见顾问的锁箱一模一样。

paras.en: It usually held important decrees to be signed as well as private papers and letters from the militia and nearby kingdoms.
paras.zh: 里面通常放着待签的重要法令，以及来自民兵与邻近王国的私信公文。

paras.en: It had been instilled in her since she was small that the box should never be tampered with. “May I?” she asked, her hand hovering over the latch.
paras.zh: 从小她就被告知绝不可擅动这箱子。”我可以吗？“她手悬在锁扣上问。

paras.en: Her father nodded.
paras.zh: 父亲点头。

paras.en: The lockbox was empty.
paras.zh: 锁箱是空的。

paras.en: The interior was lined with rich green velvet. “This box was made for your monarchy,” he said, and she looked up in surprise. “As you are next in line to the throne and just a few years away from coming of age, your mother and I felt it was time you had your own for safekeeping.” “Papa, it’s beautiful,” she said. “But I don’t need one now.” “No,” he said softly. “But someday you will, and we wanted you to be prepared.
paras.zh: 内里衬着厚实的绿天鹅绒。”这箱子是为你为王而制的，“他说，她惊讶抬头。”你既是王位继承人，又离成年只差几年，我和你母亲觉得，是时候让你拥有自己的箱子妥善保管了。“”爸爸，真美，“她说，”可我现在还用不上。“”不，“他轻声说，”但终有一天你会用上，我们想让你有所准备。

paras.en: Kai and the staff know the lockbox by sight and know its contents are private.
paras.zh: “凯和仆役认得这锁箱，也知道里面内容私密。

paras.en: Whatever you put inside this box is for your eyes only, Elsa.
paras.zh: ”无论你往里放什么，都只归你一人看，艾莎。

paras.en: Your secrets are safe in here.
paras.zh: “你的秘密在这里很安全。

paras.en: For now, I suggest you keep this in your chambers.” His eyes searched hers for understanding.
paras.zh: ”眼下，我建议你把它收在寝宫。“他的目光在探寻她是否明白。

paras.en: Elsa ran her fingers along the green velvet interior. “Thank you, Papa.” He placed his hand atop hers. “It may not feel like it now, but someday your whole life will change in ways you can’t possibly imagine.” He hesitated. “Promise me when it does, if I’m not here to guide you—” “Papa—” He cut her off. “Promise me that when that day comes, you will look to this box for guidance.” Look to it for guidance?
paras.zh: 艾莎指尖划过绿色天鹅绒内里。”谢谢爸爸。“他把手覆在她手上。”也许此刻感觉不到，但终有一天你的整个人生会以你无法想象的方式改变。“他顿了顿。”向我承诺，若那时我不在身旁指引你——“”爸爸——“他打断她。”向我承诺，当那一天到来，你会向这箱子寻求指引。“向它寻求指引？

paras.en: It was a box.
paras.zh: 它不过是个箱子。

paras.en: A beautiful box, but a box nonetheless.
paras.zh: 漂亮的箱子，但终究只是个箱子。

paras.en: Still, it was a big step to be given a lockbox like the ones Papa and the kings and queens before him had used. “I promise,” she said.
paras.zh: 不过，获赠像爸爸及历代君王所用那般的锁箱，是迈了一大步。”我承诺，“她说。

paras.en: He kissed her on the forehead. “Put it somewhere safe.” Elsa picked up the box and walked to her parents’ bedroom door.
paras.zh: 他吻了她的额头。”把它收在稳妥处。“艾莎捧起箱子，走向父母卧室的门。

paras.en: Papa followed her into the hallway, watching her. “I will,” she promised.
paras.zh: 爸爸跟她进了走廊，目送她。”我会的，“她承诺。

paras.en: Papa smiled, and went back to his work in the library.
paras.zh: 爸爸微笑，回图书室继续他的事。

paras.en: Elsa walked back to her room with the lockbox nestled in her arms.
paras.zh: 艾莎抱着锁箱走回房间。

paras.en: The air was warm, and though little breeze came through the open windows, the sounds of the village drifted inside.
paras.zh: 空气温暖，尽管敞开的窗里微风不进，村中的声响却飘入室内。

paras.en: Elsa lingered at a nearby window, staring over the castle walls and the courtyard to the world beyond.
paras.zh: 艾莎在窗边流连，越过城堡围墙与庭院望向外面的世界。

paras.en: The village was alive and full of people.
paras.zh: 村镇生机勃勃，满是人群。

paras.en: Horses and carriages came and went.
paras.zh: 马匹与马车来来往往。

paras.en: The fountain that held their statue near the castle gates shot water high into the air like a geyser.
paras.zh: 城堡门前立着他们雕像的喷泉，喷出水柱冲天，宛如间歇泉。

paras.en: Children were splashing in the fountain fully dressed, trying to stay cool.
paras.zh: 孩子们衣衫完整地在水池里戏水，想凉快些。

paras.en: She watched as a mother pulled her son out of the fountain and scolded him.
paras.zh: 她看着一位母亲把儿子从池中拉出，训斥一番。

paras.en: Despite the tongue-lashing, the boy looked like he was having fun.
paras.zh: 尽管挨了训，男孩看上去玩得正欢。

paras.en: When was the last time Elsa had done that?
paras.zh: 艾莎上一次这样玩，是什么时候？

paras.en: She wished Mama were there to have tea with that afternoon.
paras.zh: 她多希望那天下午妈妈在，能一起喝茶。

paras.en: It was a pity to sit alone in the castle on such a warm summer afternoon.
paras.zh: 这样温暖的夏日午后，独坐城堡实在可惜。

paras.en: Where was Mama on a day this spectacular?
paras.zh: 如此明媚的一天，妈妈在哪？

paras.en: Why hadn’t she let Elsa join her? “Do you need something, Princess Elsa?” Gerda asked. “Water, perhaps?
paras.zh: 为何不让艾莎同去？”公主殿下，可需要些什么？“格尔达问，”或许来点水？

paras.en: It’s so hot today!” Like Kai, Gerda had been around since before Elsa was born.
paras.zh: “今天可真热！”和凯一样，格尔达在艾莎出生前就在了。

paras.en: She made sure Elsa was always well taken care of.
paras.zh: 她确保艾莎总被照料得妥妥帖帖。

paras.en: At the moment, she was carrying a tray of goblets with cold water.
paras.zh: 此刻她端着一盘盛冷水的酒杯。

paras.en: Elsa suspected they were for her father and the Duke. “Thank you, Gerda, I’m fine,” Elsa said.
paras.zh: 艾莎猜那是给父亲和公爵的。“谢谢格尔达，我没事，”艾莎说。

paras.en: Gerda hurried past. “Okay.
paras.zh: 格尔达匆匆走过。“好。

paras.en: As long as you’re staying cool.
paras.zh: ”只要你别热着。

paras.en: I don’t want you overheating!” Elsa kept walking, holding the box tighter.
paras.zh: “我可不想你中暑！”艾莎继续走，把箱子抱得更紧。

paras.en: She needed to find something to do to pass the time till Mama returned.
paras.zh: 她得找点事做，消磨到妈妈回来。

paras.en: Maybe Gerda was right: she needed to stay cool.
paras.zh: 也许格尔达说得对：她得凉快些。

paras.en: She could take a walk around the courtyard.
paras.zh: 她可以去庭院走走。

paras.en: Or perhaps she’d read for a spell.
paras.zh: 或者读会儿书。

paras.en: Her father had given her some books to look over that explained arrangements Arendelle had with other kingdoms.
paras.zh: 父亲给了她些书翻阅，里面讲着阿伦黛尔与其他王国的协定。

paras.en: She knew he wanted her to become familiar with things for the future, but at the moment, reading up on the kingdom’s dealings didn’t sound like fun at all.
paras.zh: 她知道他想让她为将来熟悉这些，可此刻读王国事务一点趣味也没有。

paras.en: Elsa opened the doors to her room and made her way to her childhood desk.
paras.zh: 艾莎推开房门，走到童年时的书桌前。

paras.en: She placed the lockbox on top of it, staring at it for a moment.
paras.zh: 她把锁箱放上桌面，凝视片刻。

paras.en: Alongside her things, the green box looked out of place.
paras.zh: 与她的物件摆在一起，这绿箱显得格格不入。

paras.en: Maybe a box that sacred wasn’t meant to be out in the open.
paras.zh: 也许这般神圣的箱子，本不该摊在明处。

paras.en: What important papers did she have to place in it?
paras.zh: 她有什么要紧文件可放进去？

paras.en: What correspondence did she engage in?
paras.zh: 她又与谁通信？

paras.en: No, for now she wasn’t queen.
paras.zh: 不，眼下她还不是女王。

paras.en: The box wasn’t needed, and hopefully it wouldn’t be for a very long time.
paras.zh: 这箱子用不上，但愿很久都不会用。

paras.en: She took it to her hope chest, her right hand grazing the letter E hand-painted on the lid, and placed it safely inside, covering it with a quilt her mother had made her when she was a baby.
paras.zh: 她把它拿到自己的希望之箱前，右手拂过盖上手绘的字母E，稳妥地放进去，用母亲在她婴儿时缝的被子盖上。

paras.en: Then she closed the lid.
paras.zh: 随即合上箱盖。

paras.en: A moment later, Elsa grabbed a book from her nightstand, the lockbox all but forgotten.
paras.zh: 片刻后，艾莎从床头柜抓了本书，几乎把锁箱忘到了脑后。

paras.en: Elsa heard knocking and woke with a start.
paras.zh: 艾莎听到敲门声，猛地惊醒。

paras.en: The late-afternoon sun was casting shadows that tiptoed along the walls.
paras.zh: 午后将尽的阳光投下阴影，沿墙悄悄挪移。

paras.en: She must have fallen asleep reading.
paras.zh: 她定是读着读着睡着了。

paras.en: Gerda poked her head into the room. “Oh, Princess Elsa!” she said in surprise. “I didn’t mean to wake you.
paras.zh: 格尔达探头进屋。“哎呀，艾莎公主！”她惊讶地说，“我本不想吵醒你。

paras.en: I was just coming to get you for supper before I called on your parents.” “It’s all right.
paras.zh: ”我正要来叫你用晚膳，再去请你的父母。“”没事。

paras.en: I’m up,” Elsa said, stretching her arms wide.
paras.zh: “我起来了，”艾莎说着，舒展双臂。

paras.en: If her parents were joining her for dinner, that meant her father’s meeting with the Duke of Weselton was done and her mother had returned. “Why don’t I call on them for you?” Gerda walked to Elsa’s bed and started to smooth out the quilt and fix the pillows. “Thank you, Princess!” Elsa’s room was above her parents’ chambers, which were above the Great Hall, where dinner would be served.
paras.zh: 父母若来陪她用膳，说明父亲与韦塞尔顿公爵的会面已毕，母亲也已归来。“不如我去请他们？”格尔达走到艾莎床边，抚平被子、摆好枕头。“谢谢你，公主！”艾莎的房间在父母寝宫之上，而寝宫又在大厅之上，晚膳将在大厅备好。

paras.en: While Gerda tidied up, Elsa headed down the stairs and stopped short when she heard them arguing.
paras.zh: 格尔达收拾时，艾莎下楼，听见他们争吵，猛地停住。

paras.en: Her parents never fought, and she was so surprised, she wound up eavesdropping. “There must be something we can do!
paras.zh: 父母从不吵架，她太惊讶，竟听了起来。“我们总得做点什么！

paras.en: We can’t continue like this!” It was her mother talking. “Iduna, we’ve been over this time and time again.” Her father sounded frustrated. “We don’t have a choice.
paras.zh: ”不能这样下去了！“是母亲在说。”伊杜娜，这事我们翻来覆去说了多少遍。“父亲听起来很沮丧。”我们别无选择。

paras.en: We must wait.” “I’m tired of waiting!
paras.zh: “我们必须等。”“我等够了！

paras.en: We’ve lived like this for far too long!” “When it comes to magic, there is no timeline.
paras.zh: ”我们这样活得太久了！“”说到魔法，可没有时间表。

paras.en: He warned us about this.” Magic?
paras.zh: “他早警告过我们。”魔法？

paras.en: Magic was part of a child’s imagination.
paras.zh: 魔法本是孩童的想象。

paras.en: The stuff of storybooks.
paras.zh: 是童话书里的东西。

paras.en: Why would her parents be talking about something that didn’t exist? “We were desperate.
paras.zh: 父母为何要谈不存在之物？“那时我们走投无路。

paras.en: We didn’t think.
paras.zh: ”我们没多想。

paras.en: We should have tried to change their fates.
paras.zh: “我们本该试着改变他们的命运。

paras.en: Maybe if we appealed to Grand Pabbie again…” “No!
paras.zh: ”或许我们再求求皮比……“”不！

paras.en: We can’t be seen there.
paras.zh: “我们不能去那里被人看见。

paras.en: Even your travels to the village are getting too risky.
paras.zh: ”连你去村里的行踪都越来越危险。

paras.en: What if someone learned where you were going?
paras.zh: “万一有人知道你要去哪？

paras.en: Who you were seeing?
paras.zh: ”你在见谁？

paras.en: Do you know what would happen if she were brought here?” Who are they talking about?
paras.zh: “你可知道若把她带来这里会怎样？”他们说的“她”是谁？

paras.en: Elsa strained to hear more.
paras.zh: 艾莎努力想听更多。

paras.en: Was this about where Mama disappeared to on her outings?
paras.zh: 这是关于妈妈出门时去了哪吗？

paras.en: Nothing they were saying made sense. “I am always discreet, and I won’t stop visiting.” Her mother sounded defiant. “We’ve missed so much already.” “It was the only way.
paras.zh: 他们说的没一句说得通。“我向来谨慎，不会停下不探。”母亲语气倔强。“我们已经错过太多。”“那是唯一办法。

paras.en: You and I both know that.
paras.zh: ”你我都心知肚明。

paras.en: The magic will break soon.” “It’s been over ten years and it hasn’t waned!
paras.zh: “魔法很快会破。”“都过去十多年了，丝毫未减！

paras.en: It isn’t fair to any of us, especially Elsa.” She perked up.
paras.zh: ”这对我们任何人都不公平，尤其是艾莎。“她一下警觉起来。

paras.en: What did this have to do with her? “Elsa is fine.” “She’s not fine, Agnarr.
paras.zh: 这和她有何干？”艾莎挺好的。“”她不好，安格瑞。

paras.en: She’s lonely.” Yes!
paras.zh: “她孤独。”对！

paras.en: Elsa wanted to cry out.
paras.zh: 艾莎想喊出声。

paras.en: I am lonely.
paras.zh: “我孤独。

paras.en: Her mother knew her innermost thoughts.
paras.zh: 母亲懂她最隐秘的心思。

paras.en: It almost made her want to cry with relief.
paras.zh: 这几乎让她如释重负，想哭出来。

paras.en: But she didn’t understand what that had to do with their argument. “We will introduce her to more people.
paras.zh: 可她不懂这跟争吵有何关系。”我们会让她多结交些人。

paras.en: The Duke of Weselton mentioned a prince he thought she might connect with.
paras.zh: “韦塞尔顿公爵提过一位王子，他觉得她或许合得来。

paras.en: We’ve let her start coming to royal outings.
paras.zh: ”我们已让她开始参加王室活动。

paras.en: The important thing is she’s safe.
paras.zh: “紧要的是她平安。

paras.en: They both are.
paras.zh: ”她们俩都平安。

paras.en: Isn’t that what we wanted?” “She deserves to know what she’s capable of, Agnarr.” “She will when the time is right.
paras.zh: “这不正是我们想要的吗？”“她该知道自己能做什么，安格瑞。”“时机成熟她自会知道。

paras.en: We haven’t seen any sign she still can—” “There you are, Princess!” Gerda came up behind her and Elsa jumped. “I was wondering if you had gotten lost.
paras.zh: ”我们还没见她仍能做到的迹象——“”你在这儿啊，公主！“格尔达从身后出现，艾莎吓了一跳。”我还以为你迷路了。

paras.en: Olina is ready to serve supper.
paras.zh: “奥丽娜备好晚膳了。

paras.en: Have you spoken to your parents?” “I…” Elsa’s cheeks flushed as her parents stepped into the hallway, looking from Elsa to Gerda.
paras.zh: ”你跟父母说过了吗？“”我……“父母走进走廊，目光在艾莎与格尔达间游移，艾莎脸颊泛红。

paras.en: Her mother kissed her forehead. “How long have you been standing there?” she asked. “I had just reached your door when Gerda arrived,” she lied.
paras.zh: 母亲吻她额头。”你站那儿多久了？“她问。”格尔达来时，我刚到门口，“她撒了谎。

paras.en: Her mother’s face relaxed. “I missed you today.” She linked arms with Elsa and started walking with her down the hall to the staircase. “I want to hear what you did while I was gone.” “Nothing much.” It was the truth, yet Elsa knew there was also much she wasn’t saying.
paras.zh: 母亲神色放松。”今天我想你。“她挽起艾莎，沿走廊走向楼梯。”我想听你在我不在时做了什么。“”没什么。“这是实话，可艾莎知道，也有许多她没说出口。

paras.en: Her parents talked about banal things on their walk to supper, but Elsa couldn’t concentrate.
paras.zh: 去用膳的路上，父母聊着琐碎事，艾莎却无法集中精神。

paras.en: She kept thinking about their argument, and what her father had said.
paras.zh: 她总想着他们的争吵，以及父亲说的话。

paras.en: Do you know what would happen if she were brought here?
paras.zh: ”你可知道若把她带来这里会怎样？“

paras.en: Elsa couldn’t help wondering: who was “she”?
paras.zh: 艾莎忍不住猜想：”她“究竟是谁？

paras.en: Her bed was warm and cozy, and that incessant knocking seemed far away.
paras.zh: 她的床温暖舒坦，那不停的敲门声似乎遥不可及。

paras.en: Anna wiped the drool from her mouth and tried to keep dreaming, but it was hard.
paras.zh: 安娜擦去嘴角的口水，想继续做美梦，可很难。

paras.en: Someone kept interrupting. “Anna?” Her name sounded like a whisper on the wind.
paras.zh: 有人不停打断。“安娜？”她的名字像风中的低语。

paras.en: It was followed by more annoying knocking. “Anna?” “Huh?” Anna pulled a piece of wet hair from her mouth and sat up. “Sorry to wake you, but…” “No, no, no, you didn’t.” Anna yawned, her eyes still closed. “I’ve been up for hours.” Normally she would have been.
paras.zh: 接着又是恼人的敲门声。“安娜？”“嗯？”安娜从嘴里抽出一缕湿发，坐起身。“抱歉吵醒你，可是……”“不不不，你没吵醒我。”安娜打着哈欠，眼睛仍闭着。“我起来好几个小时了。”平日她本该如此。

paras.en: She always rose before the sun to help her parents prepare bread.
paras.zh: 她总在日出前起身，帮父母准备面包。

paras.en: Their shop, Tomally’s Baked Goods, churned out dozens of loaves and bakery items a day.
paras.zh: 他们的店“托玛丽烘焙坊”一天能出炉几十个面包与糕点。

paras.en: But the previous night she’d had trouble sleeping and her dreams were restless.
paras.zh: 可前一夜她睡不安稳，梦境纷乱。

paras.en: She kept calling for someone, but she couldn’t remember who it was, just that she missed this person.
paras.zh: 她不停呼唤某人，却记不起是谁，只知自己思念此人。

paras.en: Anna felt herself starting to drift off again. “Anna?” She let out a loud snore and jolted awake again. “What?” “Time to get ready.
paras.zh: 安娜觉着自己又要飘回梦乡。“安娜？”她大声一鼾，又猛地惊醒。“啥？”“该准备啦。

paras.en: Freya is coming this morning.” “Of course,” Anna said, her eyes starting to close again. “Freya.” Wait.
paras.zh: ”芙蕾雅今早要来。“”当然，“安娜说，眼睛又要合上。”芙蕾雅。“等等。

paras.en: What?
paras.zh: ”什么？

paras.en: Her eyes opened wide. “Freya’s coming!” Anna practically leapt out of bed and skidded across the floor in her bare feet.
paras.zh: “她睁大眼睛。”芙蕾雅要来！“安娜几乎从床上弹起，光着脚在地板上一滑。

paras.en: She didn’t bother looking in the mirror.
paras.zh: 她懒得照镜子。

paras.en: Her long red hair, which she had unbraided the night before, couldn’t be that messy, could it?
paras.zh: 她前一晚散开的红色长发，不至于那么乱吧？

paras.en: Hmmm…maybe she’d give it a quick glance before she pulled off her nightdress.
paras.zh: 嗯……也许脱睡衣前该匆匆瞥一眼。

paras.en: She looked in the mirror.
paras.zh: 她看向镜子。

paras.en: Not good.
paras.zh: ”不好看。

paras.en: Her hair looked like a bird’s nest.
paras.zh: “她的头发像鸟窝。

paras.en: Did she have time to fix it?
paras.zh: ”她有时间打理吗？

paras.en: She had to fix it.
paras.zh: “她必须打理。

paras.en: Where was her brush?
paras.zh: ”她的梳子在哪？

paras.en: It should have been on the desk like it always was, but it wasn’t there.
paras.zh: “它该像往常一样在书桌上，却不在。

paras.en: Where was it?
paras.zh: ”它去哪了？

paras.en: Think, Anna.
paras.zh: “想想，安娜。

paras.en: She remembered brushing her hair the morning before at the window seat, because it had the best view of Arendelle.
paras.zh: 她记起前一天早上在窗边座梳头，因为那能最好地望见阿伦黛尔。

paras.en: Looking at Arendelle made her start dreaming about Arendelle and what she’d do when she someday moved there.
paras.zh: 望着阿伦黛尔，她开始遐想有朝一日搬去那里会做些什么。

paras.en: She’d have her own bake shop, of course, and her cookies would be so popular that people would be lined up day and night to purchase them.
paras.zh: 当然要有自己的烘焙店，她的饼干会红到人们日夜排队来买。

paras.en: She’d meet new people and make friends, and it all sounded so glorious she had started singing and spinning around the room with the hairbrush…Oh!
paras.zh: 她会结识新人、交到朋友，这一切听来如此美好，她竟唱着歌、拿着梳子在屋里转圈……噢！

paras.en: Now she remembered where she had flung it.
paras.zh: ”现在她记起把它甩去哪了。

paras.en: She knelt down and looked under her bed.
paras.zh: “她跪下，看向床底。

paras.en: Anna retrieved the brush and ran it through her hair as she walked around her room.
paras.zh: 安娜取回梳子，一边在房里踱步一边梳发。

paras.en: The hand-painted armoire matched the rosemaling on her desk, her bed, and her pink quilt.
paras.zh: 手绘的大衣柜与书桌、床和粉色被子的玫瑰花饰相配。

paras.en: She and her mother had painted the pieces together.
paras.zh: 这些家具是她与母亲一同漆的。

paras.en: Her father had made her the rocking chair she sat in when she read, usually while she snuggled under her soft white blanket.
paras.zh: 父亲为她做了那把读书时坐的摇椅，她通常裹着柔软的白毯窝在里面。

paras.en: But her favorite gift he’d made was the wooden Arendelle Castle he’d carved for her twelfth birthday.
paras.zh: 但她最爱的礼物，是他为她十二岁生日雕的木制阿伦黛尔城堡。

paras.en: She kept it on the window seat, where she admired it day and night.
paras.zh: 她把它摆在窗边座，日夜欣赏。

paras.en: Her pink room wasn’t large, but she loved it.
paras.zh: 她的粉色房间不算大，她却爱极了。

paras.en: Hanging on the front of the armoire was the new royal-blue apron with red and green embroidery that her mother had made her.
paras.zh: 衣柜前挂着母亲新做给她、绣着红绿花纹的宝蓝色围裙。

paras.en: She’d been saving it for Freya’s next visit, and that visit was today!
paras.zh: 她一直留着等芙蕾雅下次来访，而今天就是那天！

paras.en: Her parents were so busy with the bakery they didn’t socialize much, but her mother always made time for visits from her best friend, Freya.
paras.zh: 父母忙于烘焙，少有社交，但母亲总抽空接待挚友芙蕾雅。

paras.en: They’d been friends since they were girls, and they loved spending time together.
paras.zh: 她们自少女时便是朋友，喜欢共度时光。

paras.en: Freya usually visited them in Harmon every other month, and Anna, her mother, and Freya would spend the whole day together, baking and talking.
paras.zh: 芙蕾雅通常每隔一个月来哈蒙探望，安娜、母亲与她会整日相聚，边烤边聊。

paras.en: Anna loved hearing Freya talk about Arendelle, where she worked as a seamstress, and she loved when Freya brought her presents!
paras.zh: 安娜爱听芙蕾雅讲阿伦黛尔——她在那做裁缝——也爱芙蕾雅给她带礼物！

paras.en: There was that porcelain doll, the dark chocolate that melted on her tongue like ice, and the green silk party dress from overseas that had hung in her closet for two years.
paras.zh: 有那个瓷娃娃、在舌尖如冰般融化的黑巧克力，还有那件挂在衣柜两年、来自海外的绿色丝绸礼服。

paras.en: She didn’t have anywhere to wear a dress that nice, since she spent her days covered in flour and butter stains.
paras.zh: 她没处穿这么讲究的裙子，毕竟她整天沾满面粉和黄油渍。

paras.en: A dress like that deserved to go to a party with dancing, nice lighting, lots of talking, and no flour spills.
paras.zh: 这样的裙子该去有舞会、灯光宜人、闲谈不断、且不洒面粉的聚会。

paras.en: They had parties in the village, but Anna was one of the only fifteen-year-olds in town.
paras.zh: 村里有聚会，可安娜是镇上仅有的几名十五岁少年之一。

paras.en: She assumed Arendelle had a lot more young people than Harmon did.
paras.zh: 她猜想阿伦黛尔的年轻人定比哈蒙多得多。

paras.en: She pulled on her white dress shirt and green jumper, grabbed the apron, and finished brushing her hair, tugging at a particularly tough knot.
paras.zh: 她套上白衬衫和绿背带裙，抓起围裙，梳完头发，拽开一个特别难解的发结。

paras.en: There was another knock on the door. “Anna!” “Coming!” The sun was already starting to rise outside her window, and she had chores to do before Freya arrived.
paras.zh: 又传来敲门声。”安娜！“”来啦！“窗外太阳已升起，芙蕾雅到前她还有活儿要干。

paras.en: Freya was never late, while Anna tended to get distracted and show up a few minutes behind schedule no matter how punctual she tried to be.
paras.zh: 芙蕾雅从不迟到，安娜却总走神、比约定晚几分钟，无论她多想准时。

paras.en: Anna grabbed her shoes off the floor and hopped to the door, trying to move and get them on at the same time.
paras.zh: 安娜从地上抓起鞋，蹦跳着奔向门，边走边试图穿上。

paras.en: She almost knocked over her father, Johan, who was patiently waiting outside her door. “Papa!” Anna hugged him. “I’m sorry!” “It’s quite all right,” he said, patting her back.
paras.zh: 她差点撞倒门外耐心等候的父亲约翰。”爸爸！“安娜抱住他。”对不起！“”没事儿，“他拍着她背说。

paras.en: He was a round man, shorter than his daughter by at least a foot, and he always smelled like the mint leaves he chewed on constantly.
paras.zh: 他是个圆滚滚的男人，比女儿矮至少一英尺，身上总带着他不停嚼着的薄荷叶味。

paras.en: (He had an upset stomach most days.) He’d been bald as long as Anna could remember, but the look suited him. “Why didn’t you remind me Freya was coming?” Anna asked as she tried in vain to smooth out her hair.
paras.zh: ”（他多数日子胃不舒服。）“在安娜记忆里他一直秃顶，却很衬他。”你怎不提醒我芙蕾雅要来？“安娜徒劳地想抚平头发，问道。

paras.en: Her father’s chuckle was deep, rising from his round belly.
paras.zh: 父亲的笑声低沉，自圆滚滚的肚子升起。

paras.en: (He always said he taste-tested as many cookies as he sold.) “Anna, we told you twice last night and every day last week.” “Right!” Anna agreed, although she wasn’t sure she remembered.
paras.zh: ”（他总说尝过的饼干和卖出的一样多。）“安娜，昨晚我们说了两遍，上周每天都说了。”“对！”安娜应道，尽管她不确定自己记得。

paras.en: The day before, she had delivered two cakes to Wandering Oaken’s Trading Post and Sauna for his twins’ birthday (Anna insisted they each get their own cake), taken krumkake to the village hall for the assembly meeting, and whipped up a new batch of her famous snowman cookies to keep up with demand.
paras.zh: 前一天，她给流浪奥肯杂货桑拿店送了两个蛋糕，为他双胞胎庆生（安娜坚持各送一个），给村公所集会送了脆卷饼干，还赶制一批她出名的雪人饼干以应需求。

paras.en: They were a kid favorite, even in the summer.
paras.zh: 那是孩子们的最爱，即便在夏天。

paras.en: Freya loved them, too.
paras.zh: 芙蕾雅也爱。

paras.en: She always asked for a dozen to take back with her when she left.
paras.zh: 她离开时总讨一打带走。

paras.en: Anna wondered if there were any snowman cookies left to give her. “I should help Ma get ready,” she told her father, and hurried down the stairs.
paras.zh: 安娜想着还剩没剩雪人饼干给她。“我该帮妈妈准备，”她对边父亲，匆匆下楼。

paras.en: She ran through their cozy family room and the small kitchen, then burst through the door that led to the bakery, which was attached to their home.
paras.zh: 她跑过温馨的起居室和小厨房，冲进连着住家的烘焙坊门。

paras.en: A short woman with brown hair was already at the wooden table, mixing flour and eggs in a bowl.
paras.zh: 一位棕发矮个女人已在木桌前，往碗里拌面粉和鸡蛋。

paras.en: She looked up at Anna and smiled. “It’s about time you got down here.” Her mother kissed her cheek and pushed a strand of wispy hair behind Anna’s right ear, then straightened Anna’s apron.
paras.zh: 她抬头看安娜，微笑。“你总算下来了。”母亲吻她脸颊，把一缕细发捋到安娜右耳后，又理了理她的围裙。

paras.en: She always wanted Anna to look nice when Freya visited. “I know, I’m sorry,” Anna said, spinning around and checking the baked goods set out for purchase on the counter.
paras.zh: 她总想芙蕾雅来时安娜好看些。“知道，对不起，”安娜说着转身，查看柜台上摆出卖的糕点。

paras.en: As she’d suspected, the snowman tray was empty. “And I’m out of my cookies!
paras.zh: 如她所料，雪人盘空了。“我的饼干也没了！

paras.en: Freya loves them.” “I’m already mixing up the batter for a batch.” Her mother’s brown eyes looked tired.
paras.zh: ”芙蕾雅最爱这个。“”我已经在调一批面糊了。“母亲的棕眼透着疲惫。

paras.en: It was getting harder and harder for her to work such long hours in the bakery.
paras.zh: 她在烘焙坊连轴转，愈发吃力。

paras.en: Anna tried to compensate for the work between her studies the best she could, but her parents were insistent that she focus on her schoolwork even when school wasn’t in session.
paras.zh: 安娜尽量在功课间隙补上活儿，可父母坚持她即便放假也要专注学业。

paras.en: Papa kept telling her, “Riches come and go, but no one can take away your education.” She understood, but that meant her days were as long as theirs were sometimes: rise early; bake; do chores; go to school or do home study and work on reading, writing, and mathematics; work at the bakery; then collapse and do it all over again the next day.
paras.zh: 爸爸总说：”财富来去不定，可谁也夺不走你的教育。“她明白，可这意味着她的日子有时和他们一样长：早起、烘焙、做家务、上学或在家修习阅读写作算术、在烘焙坊干活，然后瘫倒，第二天重来。

paras.en: It didn’t leave much time for things like friends.
paras.zh: 这让她没多少时间交朋友之类。

paras.en: That was why she looked forward to Freya’s visits: they felt like a glimpse of the world beyond Harmon. “We can make some with Freya today,” her mother said. “Good idea!” Anna took a swipe of batter with her finger and licked it.
paras.zh: 正因如此她盼着芙蕾雅来访：那像窥见哈蒙之外的世界。”今天咱们和芙蕾雅一起做，“母亲说。”好主意！“安娜用手指蘸了点面糊舔掉。

paras.en: Her mother rapped her lightly with a spoon. “Sorry!
paras.zh: 母亲用勺轻敲她。”对不起！

paras.en: But you always say a cook should taste what they make.” Her mother chuckled. “True.
paras.zh: “可你总说厨子该尝自己做的。”母亲笑了。“没错。

paras.en: You certainly keep me on my toes, Anna Bear.” Anna kissed her mom on the cheek. “That’s a good thing, right?
paras.zh: ”你真让我忙个不停，安娜熊。“安娜亲母亲脸颊。”这是好事，对吧？

paras.en: Can you imagine life without me, Ma?” Her mother stopped mixing and looked at her, the smile slipping off her face.
paras.zh: “能想象没我的日子吗，妈？”母亲停下搅拌，看她，笑容从脸上褪去。

paras.en: She touched Anna’s chin. “No, I cannot.
paras.zh: 她碰了碰安娜的下巴。“不，我想象不出。

paras.en: But that day is coming, I’m sure.” Anna didn’t say anything.
paras.zh: ”可那一天会来的，我确信。“安娜没作声。

paras.en: She felt bad when her mother talked like that.
paras.zh: 母亲这样说时，她心里发酸。

paras.en: That was why she didn’t tell her about her plan to leave Harmon and move to Arendelle when she turned eighteen.
paras.zh: 正因如此，她没告诉母亲自己计划十八岁离开哈蒙、搬去阿伦黛尔。

paras.en: She loved Harmon and its people, but it was small compared to other villages, and the world was a big place.
paras.zh: 她爱哈蒙与乡亲，可比起别的村镇它太小，而世界那么大。

paras.en: She longed to see what life was like where the royal family lived. “Can you see if we have enough tea?” her mother asked.
paras.zh: 她渴望看看王室所居之地是何模样。”你看看茶够不够？“母亲问。

paras.en: Anna checked the pantry, where they kept their dry goods. “I don’t see any tea.” “Why don’t you run to the market, then?” Her mother measured a scoop of sugar out of a container and added it to the bowl. “I always like to have tea on when she arrives.
paras.zh: 安娜查了放干货的食品柜。”没看见茶。“”那你跑趟市集？“母亲从罐里舀了勺糖加入碗。”她到时我总喜欢备好茶。

paras.en: Freya has such a long journey.
paras.zh: “芙蕾雅路途那么远。

paras.en: Can you think of anything else we need?” Freya liked to set out early for her visits.
paras.zh: ”还想得起缺什么吗？“芙蕾雅总爱一早动身来探访。

paras.en: She left Arendelle before dawn, so she usually hadn’t yet had breakfast when she arrived. “Ma, do you think she’d like eggs?” Her mother smiled. “That’s a lovely idea.” Anna slipped off her shoes and put on her boots before her mother even finished the sentence.
paras.zh: 她天不亮就离开阿伦黛尔，所以到时常还没吃早饭。”妈，你觉得她会喜欢鸡蛋吗？“母亲微笑。”这主意真好。“母亲话未说完，安娜已脱鞋换靴。

paras.en: She grabbed her violet cape by the door. “I’ll be fast.” “Anna, you are never fast,” her mother said with a chuckle. “You’ll see—I’ll be quick this time.” Anna slipped out the door, took the bucket near the stoop, and headed down the street.
paras.zh: 她抓过门边的紫披风。”我会很快。“”安娜，你从不快，“母亲笑着说。”你瞧——这次我准快。“安娜溜出门，拎起门阶旁的桶，沿街走去。

paras.en: First she’d stop at the market for tea; then she’d head to the farm a little ways away for the eggs.
paras.zh: 她先去市集买茶，再去不远处农庄取蛋。

paras.en: The sky was a sea of blues, much like the ocean in the distance, and the air felt warm, but not sticky.
paras.zh: 天空是一片蓝的海，宛如远处的海洋，空气温暖却不黏腻。

paras.en: One good thing about life in the mountains, so Anna was repeatedly told, was that it was never as hot as it was in Arendelle.
paras.zh: 人们总说，山里生活的一大好处，是绝不会像阿伦黛尔那般炎热。

paras.en: Mountain air was much cooler and life was much quieter.
paras.zh: 山间空气凉爽得多，生活也安静得多。

paras.en: Anna snuck another glance at the mountainside, her eyes searching for Arendelle far below.
paras.zh: 安娜又偷瞄山腰，目光搜寻远下方的阿伦黛尔。

paras.en: She wondered what people were doing down there at that exact moment.
paras.zh: 她猜想此刻山下的人在做什么。

paras.en: Anna heard someone talking and stopped short, her bucket still swinging. “What do you want, Sven?” Ma called her a social butterfly.
paras.zh: 安娜听到有人说话，猛地停步，桶还在晃。”What do you want, Sven?“（你想要什么，斯文？）妈妈叫她”社交蝴蝶“。

paras.en: Papa called her Harmon’s official greeter.
paras.zh: 爸爸叫她哈蒙的官方迎宾员。

paras.en: She truly did like talking to people, and this was a voice she didn’t recognize from their small village.
paras.zh: 她确实爱与人交谈，而这声音在小镇上她并不熟悉。

paras.en: It was only a few rows of houses, clustered tightly together on the mountainside overlooking Arendelle.
paras.zh: 那只是几排紧紧挨着的房子，聚在山腰俯瞰阿伦黛尔。

paras.en: Each one was a different bright color—green, blue, red.
paras.zh: 每栋都是不同的亮色——绿、蓝、红。

paras.en: The bakery was orange.
paras.zh: 烘焙坊是橙色的。

paras.en: Anna knew the inhabitants of every one of those houses.
paras.zh: 安娜认识那些房子里每一户住客。

paras.en: The person speaking wasn’t one of them. “Give me a snack!” This was a second voice, much deeper than the first.
paras.zh: 说话那人不是其中任何一户。”给我点吃的！“这是第二个声音，比第一个低沉得多。

paras.en: Curious, Anna rounded the corner to the market and saw a boy about her own age standing there.
paras.zh: 出于好奇，安娜拐过街角去市集，看见一个与她年纪相仿的男孩站在那。

paras.en: He was with a large reindeer hooked up to a wagon holding big blocks of ice.
paras.zh: 他身旁拴着一头大驯鹿，拉着一辆装满大冰块的车。

paras.en: When school was in session, she met boys and girls of various ages, but she’d never seen this boy before.
paras.zh: 上学时她见过各年龄的男孩女孩，却从没见过这男孩。

paras.en: Oaken lived high in the mountains and his kids didn’t come to Harmon often, but this didn’t look like one of his children, either.
paras.zh: 奥肯住在深山，孩子不常来哈蒙，可这也不像他的孩子。

paras.en: The boy in front of her had shaggy blond hair and was wearing a deep-blue shirt with the sleeves rolled up, dark pants, and beige boots.
paras.zh: 面前这男孩一头蓬乱金发，穿深蓝衬衫、袖子卷起，配深色长裤和米色靴子。

paras.en: Most important, he seemed to be talking to a reindeer. “What’s the magic word?” he asked the reindeer.
paras.zh: 最要紧的是，他像在和驯鹿说话。”魔法咒语是什么？“他问驯鹿。

paras.en: Men moved around them, busy carrying crates of vegetables that would be sold at the market.
paras.zh: 男人们在旁穿梭，忙着搬将在市集出售的蔬菜筐。

paras.en: Anna watched the boy swipe a bunch of carrots from a crate when no one was looking.
paras.zh: 安娜看着男孩趁人不注意从筐里顺了一把胡萝卜。

paras.en: He held one high in the air above the reindeer. “Please!” he said, putting on a deeper voice.
paras.zh: 他把一根高高举到驯鹿上方。”请！“他压低嗓音说。

paras.en: Anna watched as the reindeer bit at the carrot swinging above his snout. “Ah, ah, ah!” The boy pulled the carrot away. “Share!” Next, the boy took a bite of the carrot, broke the rest in two pieces, and gave the other half to the reindeer.
paras.zh: 安娜看着驯鹿去咬鼻尖上晃的胡萝卜。”啊，啊，啊！“男孩把胡萝卜抽回。”分享！“接着男孩咬了一口，把剩下的掰成两半，另一半给了驯鹿。

paras.en: Okay, that was gross, but intriguing.
paras.zh: 好吧，是有点恶心，却也有趣。

paras.en: The boy was talking to and for the reindeer.
paras.zh: 男孩在对驯鹿说话，也替它说话。

paras.en: Strange.
paras.zh: ”奇怪。

paras.en: She couldn’t help giggling.
paras.zh: “她忍不住咯咯笑。

paras.en: The boy looked up with a start and caught her staring.
paras.zh: 男孩猛地抬头，撞见她在盯着看。

paras.en: Anna inhaled sharply.
paras.zh: 安娜倒吸一口气。

paras.en: Should she say hi?
paras.zh: 该打招呼吗？

paras.en: Run?
paras.zh: 跑？

paras.en: This was her chance to meet someone her own age—even if he had just pinched some carrots.
paras.zh: 这是她结识同龄人的机会——即便他刚偷了胡萝卜。

paras.en: She should say hi.
paras.zh: 她该打招呼。

paras.en: She stepped forward.
paras.zh: 她向前一步。

paras.en: The sound of hooves pounding against the cobblestones made her jump back.
paras.zh: 蹄子叩击石板的声响让她往后一跳。

paras.en: A wagon squeaked to a stop in front of her, and men quickly began unloading vegetables and taking them into the market.
paras.zh: 一辆马车吱呀停在她面前，男人们很快卸下蔬菜搬入市集。

paras.en: I need to get tea and eggs!
paras.zh: ”我得去买茶和蛋！

paras.en: Look at me getting distracted.
paras.zh: “瞧我分心成这样。

paras.en: She had promised her mother she would hurry, and there she was, dawdling again.
paras.zh: 她答应母亲要快，却又不紧不慢磨蹭起来。

paras.en: Still, maybe she could say hello on her way into the market.
paras.zh: 不过，进市集时或许能打个招呼。

paras.en: She walked around the horses to see the boy.
paras.zh: 她绕过马去看那男孩。

paras.en: He was gone.
paras.zh: 他人不见了。

paras.en: Not meant to meet, I guess.
paras.zh: ”多半是缘分到不了，我猜。

paras.en: Anna sighed, but she didn’t have time to linger.
paras.zh: 安娜叹气，却没空逗留。

paras.en: She ran inside to purchase the tea, put it in her bag, and then ran down the road with her bucket.
paras.zh: 她跑进去买了茶装进包，然后拎桶沿路奔去。

paras.en: Mrs.
paras.zh: 阿加德太太——

paras.en: Aagard, the cobbler’s wife, was sweeping her stairs. “Good morning, Mrs.
paras.zh: “鞋匠的妻子，正在扫台阶。”早上好，阿加德太太

paras.en: Aagard!” Anna called. “Morning, Anna!
paras.zh: “！”安娜招呼。“早上好，安娜！

paras.en: Thanks again for the bread yesterday,” the woman said. “My pleasure.” Anna rushed onward, past another row of homes, and found her way to the farm where they kept their chicken coop.
paras.zh: ”再次谢谢昨天的面包，“那女人说。”我的荣幸。“安娜继续赶路，经过另一排房屋，找到养鸡的农庄。

paras.en: She opened the netting to collect a fresh batch of eggs. “Morning, Erik, Elin, and Elise,” she greeted the hens. “I’ve got to move quick today.
paras.zh: 她掀开网罩收了一拨新鲜蛋。”早上好，埃里克、艾琳、艾莉丝，“她向母鸡们问好，”今天我得麻利点。

paras.en: Freya is coming!” She gathered at least a dozen eggs, closed up the coop, and carefully carried the bucket and the tea back to the house.
paras.zh: “芙蕾雅要来！”她收了至少一打蛋，关好鸡舍，小心拎着桶和茶回屋。

paras.en: An older man was pulling a cart with flowers down the street. “Morning, Anna!” “Morning, Erling!” Anna called. “Gorgeous blooms today.
paras.zh: 一位老人拉着花车沿街走。“早上好，安娜！”“早上好，埃林！”安娜喊。“今天花真美。

paras.en: Do you have my favorite?” Erling produced two stems of golden crocuses.
paras.zh: ”有我的最爱吗？“埃林拿出两枝金色藏红花。

paras.en: The yellow flowers were as bright as the sun.
paras.zh: 黄花亮得像太阳。

paras.en: Anna inhaled their sweet aroma. “Thank you!
paras.zh: 安娜深吸甜香。”谢谢！

paras.en: Come by later for some fresh bread.
paras.zh: “晚点来拿新鲜面包。

paras.en: First batch should be out of the oven midmorning.” “Thank you, Anna!
paras.zh: ”头炉上午中段就该出炉了。“”谢谢你，安娜！

paras.en: I will!” he said, and Anna hurried along, trying not to crack the eggs or stop again.
paras.zh: “我会的！”他说，安娜匆匆前行，尽量不磕破蛋、不再停步。

paras.en: She had a habit of stopping to talk.
paras.zh: 她有停下攀谈的习惯。

paras.en: A lot. “Ma!
paras.zh: 常常如此。“妈！

paras.en: I got the eggs and the tea!
paras.zh: ”我拿到蛋和茶了！

paras.en: Is Freya here yet?” Anna called, walking through the door.
paras.zh: “芙蕾雅到了吗？”安娜进门喊道。

paras.en: Before she could close it, a carriage pulled up in front of the house.
paras.zh: 她还没关上门，一辆马车停在屋前。

paras.en: Freya had arrived.
paras.zh: 芙蕾雅到了。

paras.en: Anna and her mother hurried to greet their guest.
paras.zh: 安娜与母亲赶忙迎接客人。

paras.en: As always, her mom’s best friend had arrived in a carriage with two men who waited while she visited.
paras.zh: 如常，妈妈这位挚友乘马车而来，两名车夫在旁等候。

paras.en: Freya had explained to Anna once that she felt safer traveling with trusted drivers, since she didn’t have her husband or her daughter accompanying her.
paras.zh: 芙蕾雅曾向安娜解释，有可信车夫同行她更安心，因丈夫与女儿并未随行。

paras.en: The pair watched as the first driver helped the woman in a dark hooded cape out of the carriage.
paras.zh: 两人看着头一位车夫扶那位披深色兜帽斗篷的女子下车。

paras.en: She quickly walked inside the bakery and shut the door, removing her hood. “Tomally!” Freya said warmly, embracing her friend.
paras.zh: 她快步走进烘焙坊关上门，掀开兜帽。“托玛丽！”芙蕾雅热情地拥抱朋友。

paras.en: The two always hugged for so long when they saw each other Anna worried she’d never get a turn.
paras.zh: 两人一见面总抱很久，安娜担心自己永没轮上。

paras.en: Anna’s mother had told her that when Anna was adopted as a baby, Freya was the first one she’d called to come see her.
paras.zh: 安娜母亲说过，安娜还是婴儿被收养时，第一个被叫来探望的就是芙蕾雅。

paras.en: Anna and Freya had spent so much time together over the years that Anna considered her an aunt.
paras.zh: 这些年来安娜与芙蕾雅相处甚多，安娜把她当姑姨一般。

paras.en: She couldn’t imagine life without her.
paras.zh: 她无法想象没有她的生活。

paras.en: Freya and Tomally finally parted, and Freya looked at Anna, her face warm with emotion. “Anna,” she said softly, and opened her arms.
paras.zh: 芙蕾雅与托玛丽终于分开，芙蕾雅看向安娜，脸上溢着温情。“安娜，”她柔声张开双臂。

paras.en: Freya always smelled sweet, like purple heather.
paras.zh: 芙蕾雅身上总有甜香，像紫色石楠。

paras.en: Anna ran into her arms and squeezed.
paras.zh: 安娜扑进她怀里紧紧抱住。

paras.en: She was a hugger.
paras.zh: 她是个爱抱人的人。

paras.en: She couldn’t help it. “It’s so good to see you!” Freya stepped back, holding Anna by the shoulders, and looked at her intently. “Have you gotten taller?
paras.zh: 她忍不住。“见到你真好！”芙蕾雅退后，双手扶着安娜肩，仔细打量。“你长高了吗？

paras.en: Tomally, is she taller?
paras.zh: ”托玛丽，她长高没？

paras.en: She’s definitely taller!” “I’m not taller,” Anna said, and they all laughed. “I was the same height two months ago.
paras.zh: “她肯定长高了！”“我没长高，”安娜说，众人都笑。“两个月前我就这身高。

paras.en: I think. ” “You look bigger,” Freya decided.
paras.zh: ”我想。“ ”你看着壮实了，“芙蕾雅断定。

paras.en: She hung her cape by the door and removed her bonnet, revealing her beautiful dark brown hair.
paras.zh: 她把斗篷挂在门边，摘下软帽，露出美丽的深棕发。

paras.en: Anna always loved her dresses.
paras.zh: 安娜总爱她的裙子。

paras.en: The one she wore that day was dark green with yellow-and-blue trim and embroidered red flowers.
paras.zh: 那天她穿的那条深绿底，镶黄蓝边，绣红花的。

paras.en: Anna wondered if Freya had made it herself.
paras.zh: 安娜猜想那是芙蕾雅自己做的。

paras.en: She was a seamstress and always brought Anna new gowns. “Or maybe it’s just that you’re getting older.” “I am fifteen,” Anna admitted.
paras.zh: 她是裁缝，总给安娜带新裙。”或许只是你长大了。“”我十五了，“安娜承认。

paras.en: Freya smiled softly. “That must be it.
paras.zh: 芙蕾雅温柔一笑。”准是这样。

paras.en: You’re becoming a young woman.” She looked at Tomally. “You’ve done a fine job raising her.” Tomally took Freya’s hand and they looked at each other fondly. “It’s been my honor.
paras.zh: “你正长成少女。”她看托玛丽。“你把她教养得真好。”托玛丽握住芙蕾雅的手，两人温情相望。“是我的荣幸。

paras.en: She’s been the most wondrous gift.” “Ma.” Anna rolled her eyes.
paras.zh: ”她是最奇妙的礼物。“”妈。“安娜翻了个白眼。

paras.en: She hated when her mother got all emotional like that.
paras.zh: 她讨厌母亲那样动情。

paras.en: She and Freya always cried at some point when they got together. “Sorry, sorry.” Tomally busied herself at the table. “You must be hungry.
paras.zh: 她与芙蕾雅相聚总会在某刻落泪。”抱歉，抱歉。“托玛丽忙着收拾桌子。”你一定饿了。

paras.en: Anna wanted to make you breakfast.” “I want to make you breakfast, too,” Anna said to her mother. “They get too busy to eat,” she told Freya, who sat down at the table alongside Tomally as Anna heated up a pan and cracked eggs into it for a quick scramble. “How is business?
paras.zh: 安娜想给你做早饭。“”我也想给妈妈做早饭，“安娜对母亲说。”他们忙得顾不上吃，“她对坐下的芙蕾雅说，安娜热锅打蛋快速炒散。”生意如何？

paras.en: Good, I hope?” Freya asked. “We love it, but it has grown, thanks to some of Anna’s specialties, and the orders have, too.” “And how is your tutoring going, Anna?” Freya asked. “It’s fine,” Anna said with a sigh, moving the eggs around the pan. “I prefer when school is in session, because I like seeing people.
paras.zh: “但愿不错？”芙蕾雅问。“我们热爱它，不过生意做大了，多亏安娜的几样拿手，订单也多了。”“你的课业怎样，安娜？”芙蕾雅问。“还行，”安娜叹气拨弄着蛋，“我更喜欢上学时，因为爱见人。

paras.en: Doing my studies with Ma is not as fun.
paras.zh: ”和妈妈在家修习没那么有趣。

paras.en: No offense.” Freya and Tomally exchanged small smiles. “Well, that may be, but your studies are important, especially history and science.” Freya always wanted to make sure Anna was applying herself, which was sweet, but what Anna really wanted to hear about was her life. “So tell us what’s going on down the mountain.
paras.zh: “无意冒犯。”芙蕾雅与托玛丽相视浅笑。“也许，可你的学业重要，尤其历史与科学。”芙蕾雅总想确保安娜用功，这很贴心，可安娜真正想听的是她的生活。“跟我们说说山下的情况吧。

paras.en: How is Arendelle?
paras.zh: ”阿伦黛尔怎样？

paras.en: Are there any festivals going on or parties to attend?
paras.zh: “有节庆或聚会可去吗？

paras.en: Do you ever see the king and the queen when you’re in the castle?
paras.zh: ”你在城堡时可曾见到国王和王后？

paras.en: Or the princess?” Freya’s face froze, and Anna wondered what she’d said wrong.
paras.zh: “或公主？”芙蕾雅脸色一僵，安娜疑惑自己说错了什么。

paras.en: Tomally patted Anna’s hand. “I think your aunt has had a long journey.
paras.zh: 托玛丽拍拍安娜的手。“我想你姑姨路途劳顿。

paras.en: Maybe we could save the questions for later.
paras.zh: ”或许问题留到稍后。

paras.en: Let’s have breakfast, then bake, shall we?” Anna nodded.
paras.zh: “我们先吃早饭，再烘焙，好吗？”安娜点头。

paras.en: A short while later, they were all covered in flour. “Anna, do you have to use so much flour?” her mother asked, waving a cloud of dust away from her face. “I hate when the cookies stick, Ma, you know that.” Anna sifted more flour onto the wooden table that doubled as a workspace.
paras.zh: 不一会儿，三人全沾满面粉。“安娜，你非用那么多面粉吗？”母亲挥开面前的粉尘问。“我讨厌饼干粘底，妈，你懂的。”安娜又往兼作案板的木桌筛了些面粉。

paras.en: She loved flour and she used it liberally, but it did make cleanup much harder.
paras.zh: 她爱面粉，用得大方，可清理确实更难。

paras.en: The bakery wasn’t large and it wasn’t bright; the windows were high up, just below the ceiling eaves.
paras.zh: 烘焙坊不大也不亮，窗高悬，恰在檐下。

paras.en: Anna had to squint to see her measurements.
paras.zh: 安娜得眯眼才看清用量。

paras.en: Spoons and pots hung on the walls, and the large wooden table stood in the middle of the room, where Anna and her mom baked bread, cinnamon rolls, and Anna’s famous cookies.
paras.zh: 勺与锅挂在墙上，大木桌立屋中，安娜和妈妈在那烤面包、肉桂卷和她出名的饼干。

paras.en: The majority of the bakery was taken up by the cast-iron stove.
paras.zh: 烘焙坊大半被铸铁炉占着。

paras.en: It was as beautiful as it was functional, and Anna was constantly tripping over it—or falling into it, hence the small burn marks on her forearms.
paras.zh: 它美观又实用，安娜却总被它绊倒——或撞上去，因此前臂上有小块烫痕。

paras.en: Those also came from paddling the bread into and out of the oven.
paras.zh: 那些也来自把面包送进送出烤箱。

paras.en: Her parents said she was the best at knowing when the temperature of the stove was just right for baking the softest bread.
paras.zh: 父母说她最懂何时炉温正好，能烤出最软的面包。

paras.en: Maybe she was a little messy when she baked, but it didn’t bother her.
paras.zh: 也许她烘焙时有点乱，她却不在意。

paras.en: She lifted her sifter again, and flour flew through the air, making Freya sneeze. “Sorry!” “Don’t apologize,” said her aunt as she pulled out her handkerchief.
paras.zh: 她又举起筛子，面粉飞扬，惹得芙蕾雅打喷嚏。“对不起！”“别道歉，”姑姨掏出手帕说。

paras.en: Anna noticed it had the Arendelle crest embroidered on it.
paras.zh: 安娜注意到上面绣着阿伦黛尔家徽。

paras.en: Anna dropped a large ball of dough onto the table, then took another fistful of flour. “I just love to watch flour fall.
paras.zh: 安娜把一大团面扔上桌，又抓一把面粉。“我就是爱看面粉飘落。

paras.en: It reminds me of snow.” Freya’s blue eyes dimmed. “Do you like the snow?” Anna patted the flour onto the dough, then used her rolling pin to flatten it. “I do!
paras.zh: ”它让我想起雪。“芙蕾雅蓝眼一暗。”你喜欢雪吗？“安娜把面粉拍上面团，用擀面杖压平。”喜欢！

paras.en: We get a lot of it up here in the mountains, obviously, and I’ve always been fond of ice-skating, playing in the snow, and making a good snowman.” “Of all your cookies, this has always been my favorite,” her aunt said, staring fondly at the tin snowman cutters on the table. “When did you start making the snowmen?
paras.zh: “山里自然雪多，我一直爱滑冰、玩雪、堆好雪人。”“你所有饼干里，这一直是我最爱，”姑姨深情盯着桌上锡制雪人模具，“你何时开始做雪人？

paras.en: Last year?” “Yes.” Anna held up a cookie cutter. “I feel like I know him.
paras.zh: ”去年？“”对。“安娜举起模具。”我觉得我认得他。

paras.en: Not know him know him, but I’ve seen him before.” “How so?” Freya asked.
paras.zh: “不是真认得，但我以前见过。”“怎见得？”芙蕾雅问。

paras.en: The snowman in her mind’s eye always had a large bottom, a smaller middle snowball section, and an oval head, with two twig arms.
paras.zh: 她心里的雪人总是一个大底、较小的中段雪球，加椭圆脑袋，两根树枝手臂。

paras.en: She liked him to have a carrot nose and three coal buttons, with royal frosting.
paras.zh: 她喜欢他胡萝卜鼻、三颗煤纽扣，配皇家糖霜。

paras.en: He looked happy and friendly. “I see him in my dreams.
paras.zh: 他看着快乐友善。“我在梦里见他。

paras.en: I kept drawing him over and over again, so finally Papa said he’d make me a cookie cutter that resembled him.
paras.zh: ”我一遍遍画他，终于爸爸说给我做个像他的饼干模。

paras.en: I make so many cookies now that Papa’s had to make dozens of cutters.
paras.zh: “如今我做的饼干太多，爸爸不得不做了几十个模具。

paras.en: We sold out of the cookies yesterday.
paras.zh: ”昨天饼干卖光了。

paras.en: Who knew this many people liked snowmen in the summer?” Her aunt smiled. “I’m happy to help you make more cookies.
paras.zh: “谁料夏天这么多人爱雪人？”姑姨微笑。“我很乐意帮你多做些饼干。

paras.en: I enjoy watching you work.
paras.zh: ”我爱看你做。

paras.en: Your mother is right—you’re a wonderful baker.” “Anna created the recipe for this dough herself,” her mother said proudly. “Did you?” Freya asked.
paras.zh: “你妈妈说得对——你是个出色的烘焙师。”“这面团配方是安娜自己创的，”母亲骄傲地说。“真的？”芙蕾雅问。

paras.en: Anna nodded. “I like to experiment.
paras.zh: 安娜点头。“我爱试验。

paras.en: I’ve picked up my mother’s love of baking.” “I see that.” Freya watched Anna carefully use a knife to lift the snowmen off the table and place them on a baking sheet.
paras.zh: ”我承了妈妈对烘焙的爱。“”看得出。“芙蕾雅看安娜小心用刀把雪人铲起放烤盘。

paras.en: Anna looked up. “You never told me how everyone liked the sirupskake.” “It was splendid!” she said, her smile returning. “Your fa— my husband asked that you bake another one soon for me to bring him.” Freya was always tripping over her words like that.
paras.zh: 安娜抬头。”你从没说大家多喜欢那 sirupskake（糖浆蛋糕）。“”棒极了！“她笑容回来，”你爸——我丈夫说让你快再烤一个，我带给他。“芙蕾雅总这样说话打磕绊。

paras.en: Anna did the same thing herself.
paras.zh: 安娜自己也常这样。

paras.en: She chalked it up to wanting to say so much in a short amount of time.
paras.zh: 她把这归因为想在短暂时间里说太多话。

paras.en: She was like a pot of melting chocolate: the words bubbled over. “Did he like the candied oranges I placed on top?” “Yes!
paras.zh: 她像一锅融化的巧克力：话语冒泡溢出。”他喜欢我放顶上的糖渍橙子吗？“”喜欢！

paras.en: He said he’d never seen it done that way before.” Anna shrugged. “I love to put my own spin on recipes.
paras.zh: “他说从没见过那样做。”安娜耸肩。“我爱给配方加点自己的花样。

paras.en: I like to be unique, if you haven’t noticed.” “I have.” Freya smiled. “I think my husband would enjoy meeting you.
paras.zh: ”我喜欢独特，你没发现吧。“”我发现了。“芙蕾雅微笑。”我想我丈夫会乐意结识你。

paras.en: You and I have a similar joyful spirit, while he”—she sighed—“carries the weight of the world on his shoulders, I’m afraid.
paras.zh: “你我有相似的快乐天性，而他——”她叹气——“怕是扛着全世界的重担。

paras.en: Much like my daughter.” Freya talked about her daughter a lot but unfortunately never brought her along for visits.
paras.zh: ”很像我女儿。“芙蕾雅常提起女儿，却遗憾从没带她同来。

paras.en: From what Anna knew, the girl seemed whip smart and serious.
paras.zh: 据安娜所知，那女孩机敏又认真。

paras.en: Anna wished she could meet her so she could shake her up a bit.
paras.zh: 安娜希望见她，好让她活泼点。

paras.en: Everyone needed to let their hair down sometimes.
paras.zh: 人人都该偶尔放松下。

paras.en: Plus it would be nice to have a friend close to her own age.
paras.zh: 况且有个年纪相仿的朋友也好。

paras.en: The clock in the kitchen chimed and Anna looked up.
paras.zh: 厨房的钟敲响，安娜抬头。

paras.en: The first batch of cookies would be ready any moment; then it would be time to put in another tray.
paras.zh: 头炉饼干随时好；接着该放另一盘。

paras.en: After that, there were four different types of bread, krumkaker (she wouldn’t fill them with cream in this heat), and at least two spice cakes to make.
paras.zh: 之后还有四种面包、脆卷（天热她不填奶油），以及至少两个香料蛋糕要做。

paras.en: Her mother hated the idea of her baking cakes that might not sell (“The ingredients cost money”), but Anna knew people would want them, and they made a tidy profit off cakes.
paras.zh: 母亲讨厌她烤可能卖不掉的蛋糕（”原料要花钱“），可安娜知道人们会要，卖蛋糕利润可观。

paras.en: It was a win-win. “You must tell him not to worry so much,” her mother said. “What is meant to be will be.” “I know.
paras.zh: 双赢。”你得告诉他别太忧心，“母亲说，”该来的终会来。“”我知道。

paras.en: I’m sure he does as well, Tomally, but sometimes the future feels so far away,” Freya said. “Then focus on now,” Anna said. “Right now you’re doing something really fun with me.” Her aunt laughed. “That is true.
paras.zh: “他定也知道，托玛丽，可有时未来遥不可及，”芙蕾雅说。“那就专注当下，”安娜说，“此刻你正和我做趣事。”姑姨笑了。“说得对。

paras.en: We are blessed in so many ways.” Anna pulled the cookies out of the oven to let them cool.
paras.zh: ”我们蒙受诸多福泽。“安娜把饼干取出炉晾凉。

paras.en: They were a light golden yellow, just how she liked them.
paras.zh: 它们呈浅金黄，正合她意。

paras.en: She always timed them perfectly. “Speaking of food, I almost forgot…” Freya dug into the woven basket she had brought and unwrapped the parchment paper.
paras.zh: 她总能把时间掐得正好。”说到吃的，我差点忘了……“芙蕾雅翻出带来的编篮，解开油纸。

paras.en: Inside was just what Anna wanted: several blocks of the darkest, thickest chocolate she’d ever seen.
paras.zh: 里面正是安娜想要的：几块她见过最黑最厚的巧克力。

paras.en: Anna lifted one to her nose.
paras.zh: 安娜拿起一块凑近鼻子。

paras.en: The chocolate smelled divine. “Thank you!
paras.zh: 巧克力香得醉人。”谢谢！

paras.en: I promise I’ll make this batch last till your next visit.
paras.zh: “我保证这批次能撑到你下次来。

paras.en: Maybe.” “Fair enough.” Freya laughed. “I may even be able to bring you some chocolate from another kingdom.
paras.zh: ”也许吧。“”说得公道。“芙蕾雅笑。”我甚至能从别的王国给你带些巧克力。

paras.en: My husband and I will be traveling the next few weeks.” “Traveling?” Anna’s eyes lit up as she placed another tray of cookies in the oven. “Where are you going?
paras.zh: “接下来几周我和丈夫要出门。”“出门？”安娜把另一盘饼干放进炉，眼睛一亮。“你们去哪？

paras.en: How are you getting there?
paras.zh: ”怎么去？

paras.en: Are you bringing your daughter?
paras.zh: “带女儿吗？

paras.en: Does she like to travel, too?
paras.zh: ”她也爱旅行吗？

paras.en: What are you wearing?” Freya started to laugh again. “So many questions!” Anna’s mother shook her head. “Always.
paras.zh: “穿什么？”芙蕾雅又笑起来。“问题真多！”安娜母亲摇头。“总是。

paras.en: The girl never stops talking.” Anna smiled. “I can’t help myself.” “We’re going alone, and our daughter is staying home with…help,” Freya said, struggling to find the right words. “The journey is long, and it will be good to have someone stay back and take care of our affairs.
paras.zh: ”这姑娘从不消停。“安娜微笑。”我忍不住。“”就我们俩去，女儿留在家，有……人照看，“芙蕾雅斟词酌句，”路途漫长，留人料理家事也好。

paras.en: She’s older than you by three years, so she’s practically an adult.” Anna began to prepare the icing by beating egg whites and powdered sugar. “I’ve never traveled before.
paras.zh: “她大你三岁，几乎算成年人了。”安娜打发蛋白和糖粉准备糖霜。“我从未出过门。

paras.en: I’ve never even been off this mountain.” “I know,” Freya said thoughtfully.
